scenario: 500M DAU 的社交平台上刷互动、垃圾私信、批量注册账号激增，真实用户开始流失。
q: 社交平台的 bot detection 系统，要解决的核心问题是什么？
options: 区分真实用户活动和自动化或恶意的 bot 活动
给用户上传的短视频自动生成对应字幕文本
压缩用户上传的图片文件来节省存储空间
训练一个通用型的开放域聊天机器人
why: Bot 会伪造账号、刷互动、发重复或有害内容，直接伤害真实用户体验和平台信任；系统目标是降低这些影响。
why_en: Bot detection exists to separate genuine user activity from automated or malicious behavior that erodes trust and experience on the platform.
options_en: Separate genuine user activity from automated or malicious bot activity.
Automatically generate matching captions for users' uploaded short videos.
Compress users' uploaded image files to save storage space.
Train a general-purpose, open-domain chatbot.
q_en: What core problem should a social-platform bot detection system solve?
scenario_en: On a 500M-DAU social platform, fake engagement, spam DMs, and bulk sign-ups are spiking, and real users are leaving.
optionExplanations: 这就是 bot detection 的目标：把伪装成人的自动化账号从真实用户里挑出来。
字幕生成是视频处理任务，和账号是否为人无关，跑题了。
图片压缩是存储优化，不涉及判断账号真伪。
训练聊天机器人是生成对话的任务，不是识别恶意账号。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the bot-detection goal: pick automated accounts posing as people out of the real user base.
Captioning is a video-processing task with no bearing on whether an account is human.
Image compression is a storage optimization, unrelated to judging account authenticity.
Training a chatbot is about generating dialogue, not spotting malicious accounts.

scenario: 面试官只给了一句"做个 bot 检测系统"，你要在定模型和阈值之前把设计边界问清楚。
q: 澄清 bot detection 需求时应主动问哪些问题？（多选）
why: 这四类答案共同决定阈值、模型复杂度和评估方式；这是对抗且标签稀缺的问题，问清楚才能定设计边界。
why_en: Clarifying prevalence, false-positive cost, latency/scale, and label capacity sets the thresholds, model complexity, and evaluation plan for an adversarial, label-scarce problem.
options: bot prevalence 和现有 heuristics 挡了多少
误判真实用户会有什么后果
检测时延要求和平台规模
人工真值标签能力
options_en: The base bot prevalence and how much existing heuristics already filter.
The consequences of wrongly flagging a real user as a bot.
The detection-latency requirement and the platform's scale.
How many verified ground-truth labels investigators can produce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于经验规则的简单判断，不是学出来的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heuristic is a hand-written rule of thumb rather than a learned model.

q_en: What should you clarify when scoping bot detection? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The interviewer just says 'build bot detection,' and you need to pin down the design boundaries before picking a model or a threshold.
optionExplanations: 问清基线 bot 占比和现有规则挡了多少，才知道新模型要在什么基础上做增量提升。
问清误伤代价，才能定出误判 guardrail 该设多严。
问清延迟要求和平台规模，才能定 serving 架构和响应速度。
问清调查员每周能出多少真值标签，才能定训练和评估能拿到多少高质量数据。
optionExplanations_en: Ask the baseline bot rate and how much existing rules already catch, so you know what floor the new model must beat.
Ask what a false positive costs, so you know how strict the guardrail needs to be.
Ask the latency bar and platform scale, so you know what serving architecture to build.
Ask how many verified labels investigators can produce weekly, so you know the label budget for training and evaluation.

scenario: 平台约有 500M DAU，人工调查员每周只能确认约数百个账号的真值标签。
q: 这组规模和标注数字，对系统设计意味着什么？
why: 决定性约束是高流量和标签稀缺并存：计算必须省着花，训练和评估都要为少量高质量标签专门设计流程。
why_en: At this scale, compute is a hard budget and the whole pipeline—training, active labeling, evaluation—has to be designed around only a few hundred trusted labels a week.
options: 计算必须是硬约束，训练和评估要专门为标签稀缺设计
标签充足，可以直接用监督学习解决全部问题
规模足够小，可以对每个账号跑最贵的模型
标注慢没关系，反正 bot 数量可以忽略不计
options_en: Compute has to be a hard constraint, and training and evaluation must be designed specifically around scarce labels.
Labels are abundant, so pure supervised learning can solve everything directly.
Scale is small enough to run the most expensive model on every account.
Slow labeling doesn't matter because bot volume is negligible anyway.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，一天内至少活跃一次的用户数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU stands for Daily Active Users, the number of unique users active on the platform in a day.

q_en: What does this scale and labeling budget imply for the design?
scenario_en: The platform has about 500M DAU, and investigators can verify only a few hundred accounts per week.
optionExplanations: 500M DAU 顶着硬算力上限，每周仅数百条标签，意味着必须走级联、主动标注、弱监督这类节省标签的路线。
现实是标签严重不足，直接监督学习覆盖不了这个规模。
500M DAU 完全谈不上「规模小」，跑不起给每个账号用最贵模型。
标注慢恰恰是核心痛点，bot 数量在这个规模下绝不可忽略。
optionExplanations_en: 500M DAU forces a hard compute budget, and only a few hundred labels a week means leaning on cascades, active labeling, and weak supervision instead of brute-force supervised training.
Reality is the opposite—labels are scarce, so pure supervised learning can't cover this scale.
500M DAU is nowhere near small enough to run the priciest model per account.
Slow labeling is exactly the core pain point, and bot volume at this scale is never negligible.

scenario: 上线三个月，靠发帖频率和 IP 黑名单拦下的 bot 占比从 80% 掉到 20%，规则本身没改。
q: 为什么说 bot detection 是一个对抗性（adversarial）问题？
why: 今天有效的频率/内容/IP 信号，明天可能被绕过；设计要偏向更难伪造的行为、图和时间模式。
why_en: Bot detection is adversarial because whatever signal catches bots today gets studied and evaded tomorrow, so design should lean on harder-to-fake behavioral and graph patterns.
options: bot 作者会持续观察系统并调整行为来逃避检测
真实用户的正常行为模式几乎永远不会变化
获取高质量新标签总是免费且即时可得的
检测系统一旦上线不会引发任何攻防博弈
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Pool[Candidate accounts] --> Boundary[Boundary cases]
  Pool --> New[New patterns]
  Boundary --> Review[Investigator review]
  New --> Review
  Review --> Eval[Gold eval set]
  Review --> Cal[Threshold calibration]
options_en: Bot authors continuously observe the system and adapt their behavior to evade detection.
Real users' normal behavior patterns almost never change at all.
High-quality new labels are always free and instantly available.
Launching a detection system never triggers any offense-defense back-and-forth.
q_en: Why is bot detection an adversarial problem?
scenario_en: Three months in, the share of bots caught by post-rate and IP-blocklist rules dropped from 80% to 20%, with the rules unchanged.
optionExplanations: 这正是对抗性的定义：攻击者会持续观察防御规则并调整行为绕过。
真实用户行为其实也会自然漂移，只是不是主动对抗。
标签依赖昂贵的人工调查，远谈不上免费即时。
上线检测通常会立刻触发攻击者反制，这才是对抗性问题的核心。
optionExplanations_en: This is the definition of adversarial: bot authors keep watching the defenses and adapt to dodge them.
Real user behavior does drift naturally too, just not as deliberate evasion.
Labels depend on expensive manual investigation, nowhere near free or instant.
Shipping a detector typically provokes an immediate reaction from attackers—that's the whole point.

scenario: 你要给 bot detection 定业务目标，不能只追求抓最多账号。
q: 更合理的业务目标是什么？
why: 决定性问题是谁承担代价：只追封禁数或 accuracy 都会激励误伤真实用户；guardrail 把体验伤害设成硬上限。
why_en: The objective should minimize bot impact on real users with a hard false-positive guardrail, because optimizing raw ban counts or accuracy alone rewards over-flagging legitimate accounts.
options: 最小化 bot 影响，设误伤上限
最大化封禁账号数量
最大化模型 accuracy
最小化人工审核数量，不管质量
whenOtherWins: 如果是已人工确认的 bot 批量清理，封禁数量可以作为执行指标而非设计主目标。
tradeoff: 抓 bot 的力度 vs 误伤真实用户的代价
options_en: Minimize bot impact, with a hard cap on false positives.
Maximize the number of banned accounts.
Maximize model accuracy.
Minimize how much manual review is needed, regardless of quality.
q_en: What is a better business objective for bot detection?
scenario_en: You are setting the business goal for bot detection, and raw account bans are not enough.
optionExplanations: 把目标定成压低 bot 造成的伤害、同时给误伤设硬上限，能持续打击 bot 又不牺牲真实用户体验。
只盯封禁数会激励系统宁可错杀，误伤真实用户。
类别严重不平衡时，高 accuracy 也可能藏着大量误判。
只压审核工作量而不管质量，会放过大量真实 bot。
optionExplanations_en: Framing the goal as minimizing bot harm with a hard cap on false positives keeps fighting bots without sacrificing real users.
Chasing raw ban counts rewards over-flagging and hurts legitimate accounts.
Under severe class skew, a high accuracy score can still hide plenty of misclassifications.
Cutting review volume regardless of quality lets many real bots slip through.

scenario: 平台上 bot 账号占比约 1%，模型全部判"人类"时 accuracy 就已经有 99%。
q: 为什么“最大化模型 accuracy”不适合作为 bot detection 的业务目标？
why: bot prevalence 和真实用户体量都很大时，高 accuracy 仍可能对应大量误判，用户感受到的是垃圾内容和误封。
why_en: Accuracy is a poor objective here because with skewed class distribution, a high accuracy score can still hide millions of real misclassifications that users feel as spam or wrongful bans.
options: 类别分布严重偏斜，用户感受到的是垃圾内容和误封
accuracy 根本无法计算
accuracy 在数学上总是等于 precision
accuracy 能自动防住对抗性攻击
options_en: Class distribution is heavily skewed, and users feel spam and wrongful bans.
Accuracy simply cannot be computed here.
Accuracy is mathematically always equal to precision.
Accuracy automatically defends against adversarial attacks.
q_en: Why is maximizing model accuracy a poor bot-detection business goal?
scenario_en: Bots are only about 1% of accounts, so a model that calls everyone human already scores 99% accuracy.
optionExplanations: 类别严重偏斜时，即使 accuracy 数字很漂亮，用户实际感受到的仍是垃圾内容和误封。
accuracy 是可以直接算出来的，问题不在能不能算。
accuracy 和 precision 定义、计算方式都不同，不能混为一谈。
指标本身不会改变攻击者的行为，防不住对抗性适应。
optionExplanations_en: Under heavy class skew, even a good-looking accuracy number can coexist with users actually feeling spam and wrongful bans.
Accuracy is trivially computable—that's not the issue here.
Accuracy and precision are defined and computed differently, so they aren't interchangeable.
A metric by itself doesn't change attacker behavior, so it can't defend against adaptation.

scenario: 风控要按不同置信度分别执行封禁、降权、限流，需要一个跨账号可比的模型输出。
q: 在这个方案里，bot detection 的核心 ML objective 是什么？
why: 主任务是预测账号是 bot 的概率（校准后的风险分数），动作层再按置信度和影响决定封禁、降权还是限流。
why_en: The core ML objective is binary classification that outputs a calibrated bot-risk score, which the action layer then turns into a ban, demotion, or rate limit.
options: 二分类：判断一个账号是不是 bot
回归预测视频播放时长
无监督聚类商品类别
生成式模型输出自然语言回复
options_en: Binary classification: decide whether an account is a bot.
Regression to predict video watch time.
Unsupervised clustering of product categories.
A generative model that produces natural-language replies.
q_en: What is the core ML objective in this bot-detection design?
scenario_en: Enforcement wants to ban, demote, or rate-limit depending on confidence, so it needs one model output comparable across accounts.
optionExplanations: 核心是账号级二分类，输出的风险分数供动作层决定封禁、降权还是限流。
预测播放时长是回归任务，和账号真伪判断无关。
商品聚类是无监督分组，bot detection 需要标签监督。
生成自然语言回复是对话任务，不是身份判别。
optionExplanations_en: It's account-level binary classification, and the risk score it outputs drives whether the action layer bans, demotes, or rate-limits.
Predicting watch time is a regression task, unrelated to judging account authenticity.
Clustering products is unsupervised grouping; bot detection needs labeled supervision.
Generating natural-language replies is a dialogue task, not identity classification.

q: 动作层更合理的选择是什么？
why: 决定性约束是不确定性和误封代价都高；软动作降低 collateral damage，只有高置信证据才升级到封禁。
why_en: When confidence is medium but the cost of wrongly banning a real user is high, demote or rate-limit first and reserve permanent bans for high-confidence evidence.
scenario: bot 分数中等但不确定，误封真实用户代价高。
options: 先降权或限流，保留高置信才封禁
所有中等分数立刻永久封禁
完全不采取任何动作
删除所有用户内容
whenOtherWins: 如果证据是高置信恶意行为且风险大，直接移除账号更合适。
tradeoff: 可逆的软动作 vs 一步到位的封禁
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Score[Medium score] --> Soft[Limit or demote]
  Soft --> Observe[Keep evidence]

flowchart LR
  Score[Medium score] --> Ban[Permanent ban]
  Ban --> FP[High FP risk]
options_en: Demote or rate-limit first, reserving bans for high-confidence cases.
Immediately and permanently ban every medium-score account.
Take no action at all.
Delete all of the account's content.
q_en: What should the action layer do in this case?
scenario_en: The bot score is medium-confidence, and wrongly banning a real user is expensive.
optionExplanations: 分数中等又不确定时，先用可逆的降权/限流控制伤害，等证据升到高置信度再封禁。
置信度不够就用最重的动作，误伤代价最高。
放着不管等于放任风险账号继续造成伤害。
删内容伤的是真实用户，也没解决账号本身的风险。
optionExplanations_en: At medium, uncertain confidence, start with reversible demotion or rate-limiting and save bans for high-confidence evidence.
Jumping to the heaviest action at insufficient confidence maximizes false-positive cost.
Doing nothing just lets a risky account keep causing harm.
Deleting content hurts real users' work without addressing the account's actual risk.

scenario: 已知 bot 家族每周被封几万个，同时每月都冒出没人见过的新脚本行为模式。
q: 为什么高层设计要同时用 supervised/non-parametric 方法和 unsupervised 方法？
why: 已见过的 bot 签名可用监督/近邻高精度覆盖；不断出现的新模式需要异常检测去找 unknown unknowns。
why_en: Known bot signatures get high-precision supervised and nearest-neighbor coverage, while unsupervised anomaly detection is there to catch new patterns nobody has labeled yet.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Known[Known bot labels] --> Sup[Supervised model]
  Known --> KNN[Nearest neighbor]
  New[New behavior] --> Anom[Anomaly detection]
  Sup --> Merge[Risk queue]
  KNN --> Merge
  Anom --> Merge
options: 已知模式用监督/近邻覆盖，未知模式靠无监督发现
所有 bot 都只能靠人工审核识别
无监督方法可以完全替代所有标签
只用内容 LLM 处理每条帖子就足够
options_en: Known patterns get supervised/nearest-neighbor coverage; unknown patterns get unsupervised detection.
All bots can only be identified through manual review.
Unsupervised methods can fully replace every label.
Running one content LLM on every post is enough.
q_en: Why use supervised or non-parametric methods together with unsupervised methods?
scenario_en: Known bot families get tens of thousands of takedowns a week, yet brand-new script patterns show up every month.
optionExplanations: 已见过的 bot 签名交给监督/近邻高精度覆盖，不断冒出来的新模式则靠无监督异常检测去发现。
调查员每周只能看数百个账号，纯人工远不够覆盖规模。
无监督结果仍需要少量标签校准和验证，替代不了全部监督。
bot 更多是行为/图协同问题，光看内容判别不够。
optionExplanations_en: Known bot signatures get high-precision supervised/nearest-neighbor coverage, while unsupervised anomaly detection surfaces the constantly emerging new patterns.
Investigators can only review a few hundred accounts a week, nowhere near enough manual coverage at this scale.
Unsupervised output still needs a few labels to calibrate and verify—it can't replace supervision entirely.
Bots are mostly a behavior/graph coordination problem, so content alone falls short.

q: 系统必须怎么处理这两类标签？
why: 模型生成的标签带反馈循环和错误传播风险；调查员标签更可信，训练、索引和评估都要分开记录来源。
why_en: Model-generated labels can create a feedback loop that amplifies the model's own mistakes, so investigator ground truth must be tracked separately and trusted more.
scenario: 近邻索引里既有调查员真值标签，也有模型自己生成的标签。
options: 区分来源并降低模型生成标签的权重
把所有标签当同等真值使用
只保留模型自己生成的标签
把人工标签全部删除
whenOtherWins: 如果自动标签来自审计过的确定性强规则，可以提高权重，但仍要标注来源。
tradeoff: 隔离错误传播 vs 索引里标签的总覆盖量
options_en: Track the source and down-weight model-generated labels.
Treat every label as equally trustworthy.
Keep only the model's own generated labels.
Delete all the human-verified labels.
q_en: How should the system treat these two label sources?
scenario_en: The nearest-neighbor index contains both investigator-confirmed labels and labels generated by the model itself.
optionExplanations: 标记标签来源、给模型自产的标签降权，能防止模型把自己的错误当真值反复放大。
两类标签可信度并不一样，等同对待会放大模型系统性错误。
扔掉调查员标签等于丢了最稀缺、最可信的信号来源。
人工标签正是唯一能校准阈值和验证效果的可信来源，删不得。
optionExplanations_en: Tagging label source and down-weighting model-generated ones stops the model from reinforcing its own mistakes as ground truth.
The two sources aren't equally trustworthy, so treating them the same amplifies the model's systematic errors.
Dropping investigator labels throws away the scarcest, most reliable signal.
Human labels are the only trustworthy source for calibrating thresholds and validating results—deleting them isn't an option.

scenario: 调查员每周只能人工确认几百个账号，这是全平台唯一可信的真值来源。
q: 调查员的人工标签最适合怎么用？
why: 人工标签稀缺，应投向最能降低不确定性的样本：决策边界、代表新模式的账号，以及支撑可信评估的测试集。
why_en: Scarce investigator labels are best spent on boundary cases and emerging patterns, then reused to build trustworthy test sets and calibrate action thresholds.
options: 验证决策边界样本、构建高质量测试集、校准阈值
随机分配标签到明显没问题的负例样本上
完全弃用这些标签，理由是数量太少了
只用来给前端界面的文案提示做微调
options_en: Validate boundary cases, build high-quality test sets, and calibrate thresholds.
Spend them randomly on obviously clean negative cases.
Discard them entirely on the grounds that the volume is too small.
Use them only to tweak front-end UI copy and hints.
q_en: What is the best use of investigator-provided human labels?
scenario_en: Investigators can only confirm a few hundred accounts a week, and that is the platform only trustworthy ground truth.
optionExplanations: 稀缺的人工标签该投向决策边界样本、构建高质量测试集，并用来校准阈值。
明显负例几乎不提供新信息，是在浪费稀缺标签。
少量高质量标签仍是评估的基石，数量少不等于没价值。
前端提示微调不是标签的核心用途，浪费了最珍贵的信号。
optionExplanations_en: Scarce human labels should go toward validating boundary cases, building a high-quality test set, and calibrating thresholds.
Obvious negatives carry almost no new information, wasting a scarce budget.
Even a small trusted set anchors evaluation—low volume doesn't mean zero value.
UI-hint tuning isn't the core use of labels; it wastes the most valuable signal available.

q: 应优先把哪些账号送去人工审？
why: 边界样本最能改善阈值和模型误差，新模式样本能帮助捕捉对抗漂移；标签预算稀缺就要花在刀刃上。
why_en: With only a few hundred labels a week, spend them on accounts near the decision boundary or representing new patterns, since those carry the most information.
scenario: 每周只能人工调查数百账号，模型分数有大量接近阈值的账号。
options: 决策边界附近，或代表新模式的账号
分数接近 0 的明显正常账号
随机抽取的热门真实用户
已经人工确认过的重复样本
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是无偏估计总体 prevalence，还需要随机/分层样本配合重加权。
tradeoff: 把稀缺标签花在信息量最高处 vs 覆盖更随机的样本
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Scores[Model scores] --> Border[Near threshold]
  Drift[Unseen cluster] --> Border
  Border --> Human[Human labels]
  Human --> Retrain[Retrain and calibrate]
options_en: Accounts near the decision boundary, or representing new patterns.
Obviously normal accounts scoring near zero.
A random sample of popular real users.
Samples that have already been confirmed by investigators.
q_en: Which accounts should be prioritized for human review?
scenario_en: Investigators can review only a few hundred accounts per week, while many accounts sit near the model threshold.
optionExplanations: 标签预算稀缺时，优先审边界附近和代表新模式的账号，因为每条标签都能显著改善阈值或模型误差。
结果几乎能预判，标了也几乎不提供新信息。
随机热门账号和风险判断无关，对分数分布没有校正作用。
答案已经知道了，重复标注不产生新知识。
optionExplanations_en: With a scarce label budget, prioritize boundary cases and emerging patterns, since each label meaningfully improves the threshold or model error.
The outcome is nearly predictable already, so labeling it adds almost no information.
Random popular accounts are unrelated to risk and barely correct the score distribution.
The answer is already known, so relabeling produces no new knowledge.

scenario: 用户举报每天几十万条，但很大一部分只是不喜欢内容而误报的真实账号。
q: 用户生成信号（举报、申诉结果等）在 bot detection 里的特点是什么？
why: 用户举报和申诉结果不是完美真值，但规模远大于调查员标签，适合弱监督训练、监控和优先级排序。
why_en: User reports and appeal outcomes are noisy compared to investigator labels, but their volume makes them useful for weak supervision, monitoring, and prioritization.
options: 噪声大但量级大，如举报和申诉结果
数量少但几乎完美
只用于前端展示，不进模型
不能和模型标签结合使用
options_en: Noisy but high-volume, like reports and appeal outcomes.
Small in volume but nearly perfect.
Used only for front-end display, never fed into the model.
Cannot be combined with model-generated labels.
q_en: What is special about user-generated signals such as reports and appeals?
scenario_en: User reports come in at hundreds of thousands a day, but many of them are real accounts flagged just because someone disliked the post.
optionExplanations: 举报和申诉本身有噪声，但量级远超调查员能给出的标签，能拿去喂弱监督模型，还能盯着趋势排优先级。
举报和申诉本身就会有误报，谈不上「几乎完美」。
这些信号能作弱监督直接进模型，不只是展示用。
按可信度加权后完全可以和模型标签融合使用。
optionExplanations_en: Reports and appeal outcomes are noisy, but their volume dwarfs investigator labels, making them useful for weak supervision, monitoring, and prioritization.
Reports and appeals carry their own error, far from 'nearly perfect'.
These signals feed the model as weak supervision, not just UI display.
Confidence-weighted, they combine perfectly well with model-generated labels.

scenario: 刚确认了一个 bot 账号，想把这个标签沿社交图扩散到它的同伙账号上。
q: 网络（图）标签可以从哪些信号传播？（多选）
why: IP 集群、行为相似度和批量注册模式能帮助发现整组协同 bot，而不只是单个账号；但要防止误差沿图传播。
why_en: Malicious IP clusters, behavioral similarity to confirmed bots, and bulk registration patterns can propagate labels across an entire coordinated bot network.
options: 已知恶意 IP 集群
与确认 bot 行为高度相似的账号
批量注册模式
浏览器字体设置
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Seed[Confirmed bot] --> IP[IP cluster]
  Seed --> Similar[Behavior similarity]
  Seed --> Signup[Bulk signup]
  IP --> Candidates[Candidate bot group]
  Similar --> Candidates
  Signup --> Candidates
options_en: Known malicious IP clusters.
Accounts whose behavior closely matches confirmed bots.
Bulk registration patterns.
Browser font settings.
q_en: Which signals can propagate labels through the network graph? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: You just confirmed one bot account and want to propagate that label across the social graph to its accomplices.
optionExplanations: 已知恶意 IP 集群能把新的可疑账号追溯出来。
行为高度相似于已确认 bot，往往代表同一场协同 campaign。
批量注册来自同一来源，是 bot 农场的典型痕迹。
浏览器字体只是界面偏好，和图上的标签传播无关。
optionExplanations_en: Known malicious IP clusters trace out new suspicious accounts.
Behavior closely matching a confirmed bot usually signals the same coordinated campaign.
Bulk registration from a shared source is a classic bot-farm footprint.
Browser font is just a UI preference, unrelated to graph label propagation.

scenario: 某类慢速 bot 全库只有 200 个确认样本，训练时正类几乎被上亿负例淹没。
q: 生成式方法合成的 bot 行为数据，主要用途是什么？
why: class imbalance 和覆盖不足是稀缺正类的核心痛点，合成数据能补时间/内容/网络维度，但要小心学到生成器伪影。
why_en: Synthetic bot behavior helps cover rare temporal, content, and network patterns given severe class imbalance, but it must be validated so the model doesn't just learn generator artifacts.
options: 补充稀有 bot 类别的多维度数据
替代所有真实线上评估
保证线上完全没有误伤
让模型从此不再需要负样本
options_en: Augments rare bot categories with more multi-dimensional data.
Replace all real online evaluation.
Guarantee zero false positives in production.
Eliminate the need for negative examples entirely.
q_en: What is the main use of synthetic bot-behavior data?
scenario_en: One slow-drip bot family has only 200 confirmed samples, so the positive class drowns in hundreds of millions of negatives.
optionExplanations: 生成式合成数据主要用来补时间/内容/网络维度的稀有 bot 类别，缓解正类覆盖不足。
合成数据不能替代真实线上评估，还得看真实数据。
合成数据不改变线上误伤风险，保证不了零误伤。
分类任务仍然需要负样本，合成数据取代不了。
optionExplanations_en: Synthetic data mainly augments rare bot categories across time, content, and network dimensions, easing scarce positive-class coverage.
Synthetic data can't replace real online evaluation.
It doesn't change live false-positive risk, so it can't guarantee zero harm.
The classification task still needs negative examples regardless.

scenario: 系统上线一年，早期靠频率规则就能抓的简单 bot 已基本绝迹，训练集仍只从线上日志采样。
q: bot detection 越做越好，训练数据会出现什么 survival bias？
why: 简单 bot 被早早过滤后，日志里留下的正例更像是能绕过系统的高难样本，模型必须持续适应这种分布变化。
why_en: As detection improves, easy bots get filtered out early, so the bots that survive to be observed are systematically harder, and the model must keep adapting.
options: 观测到的 bot 越来越难，正例天然变复杂
所有 bot 都会变得更容易识别
标签获取成本会降到零
模型从此不再需要更新
options_en: The bots that remain observable get harder, so positives grow more complex.
All bots become easier to identify.
Label-acquisition cost drops to zero.
The model no longer needs to be updated.
q_en: What survival bias appears as bot detection improves?
scenario_en: A year in, the simple bots that rate rules used to catch are basically gone, yet training data is still sampled from production logs.
optionExplanations: 简单 bot 被早早拦下后，留在日志里的正例往往是躲过了检测的难例，模型得跟着这种变化持续调整。
方向说反了：观测到的 bot 是越来越难识别，不是更容易。
标注成本不会因为检测变好而自动降低。
对抗漂移要求模型持续更新，不可能一劳永逸。
optionExplanations_en: Once easy bots get filtered out early, the positives left in the logs are systematically the hard ones that evaded detection, so the model must keep adapting.
The direction is reversed—observed bots get harder to spot, not easier.
Labeling cost doesn't fall on its own just because detection improves.
Adversarial drift means the model must keep being updated, never a one-and-done.

scenario: 攻击者能随时改文案和头像，但改不掉真人的作息和反应时间，你要挑抗漂移的特征。
q: 衡量账号「像不像人」的活动模式特征可以包括哪些？（多选）
why: 这些特征刻画「像不像人」的行为节奏，通常比内容文本更难长期伪造，是对抗漂移下更稳健的信号。
why_en: Timing intervals, reaction-time variance, session rhythms, and sudden bursts capture how human-like an account's cadence is, and they're harder to fake long-term than content.
options: 发帖/互动的时间间隔分布
点击反应时间的方差
会话时长和昼夜节律
短时间内的突增行为
options_en: The distribution of time gaps between posts or interactions.
The variance in reaction time to content.
Session duration and circadian rhythm.
Sudden bursts of activity in a short window.
q_en: Which activity-pattern features can measure whether an account looks human? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Attackers can swap copy and avatars at will but not a human sleep cycle or reaction time, so you want drift-resistant features.
optionExplanations: 发帖/互动的间隔分布刻画动作之间的节奏，是核心的行为节奏特征。
反应时间方差过小常代表按脚本执行的机器操作。
缺乏昼夜节律、作息不像人是常见 bot 信号。
短时间内的爆发往往超出人类操作速度，是可疑信号。
optionExplanations_en: Gaps between posts or interactions capture the core cadence of an account's actions.
Suspiciously low variance in reaction time often signals scripted machine behavior.
Missing circadian rhythm—no human-like sleep/wake pattern—is a common bot tell.
A short-window burst often exceeds what a human can physically do, so it's a red flag.

q: 更稳妥的窗口设计是什么？
why: 多窗口能同时捕捉爆发、日常节奏和长期异常；统计量如熵、方差能量化行为「像不像人」。
why_en: Computing features over hourly, daily, and weekly windows captures bursts, daily rhythm, and longer-term anomalies that a single window would miss.
scenario: 你计算 bot 活动特征，只看过去 1 小时会漏掉周级节律，只看一周会漏掉爆发。
options: 用小时、天、周等多个时间窗口和统计量
只保留最长的时间窗口
只保留最短的时间窗口
完全不使用时间相关特征
whenOtherWins: 如果 serving 成本极端紧张，可先用少量最高收益窗口。
tradeoff: 多窗口特征的覆盖度 vs 计算和存储成本
options_en: Compute features across multiple windows and statistics—hourly, daily, weekly.
Keep only the longest time window.
Keep only the shortest time window.
Skip time-based features entirely.
q_en: What is the safer window design for activity features?
scenario_en: You are computing bot activity features: a 1-hour window misses weekly rhythm, while a 1-week window misses bursts.
optionExplanations: 同时算小时、天、周多个窗口的统计量，能一次覆盖突发、日常节奏和长期漂移三种尺度。
单一长窗口会把短时突增这种强信号平滑掉。
单一短窗口看不到周级节律这类长期模式。
时间节奏正是难以长期伪造的稳健信号，放弃它很可惜。
optionExplanations_en: Computing stats across hourly, daily, and weekly windows at once covers bursts, daily rhythm, and long-term drift in one shot.
A single long window smooths away strong short-burst signals.
A single short window misses long-term patterns like weekly rhythm.
Timing cadence is exactly the kind of signal that's hard to fake long-term—dropping it wastes that.

scenario: 同一批 bot 每周换一次文案模板，还改用 LLM 生成帖子，内容分类器精度持续下滑。
q: 为什么内容信号在 bot detection 中通常比较弱？
why: bot 能看到自己发的内容并主动换文案或用生成式内容规避；行为和图关系更难长期伪装，是更稳健的主力信号。
why_en: Content is the most visible signal to an attacker, who can simply rewrite or generate new text to dodge detection, while behavioral and graph patterns are harder to fake over time.
options: 内容最容易被攻击者看到并主动改写来绕过检测
内容信号在这里永远没有任何参考价值
内容天生无法被向量化用于相似度比较
内容信号只对推荐排序系统才有用
tradeoff: 内容信号（可见、易规避）vs 行为/图信号（更难长期伪装）
options_en: Content is the most visible to attackers, who can rewrite it to dodge detection.
Content signals here have zero reference value under any circumstance.
Content is inherently impossible to vectorize for similarity comparison.
Content signals are useful only to recommendation ranking systems.
q_en: Why are content signals usually weaker in bot detection?
scenario_en: The same bot ring rotates its copy templates weekly and now generates posts with an LLM, so the content classifier keeps degrading.
optionExplanations: 内容是攻击者最容易看到的信号，稍微改写文案或换生成式内容就能绕过检测。
内容仍能当辅助信号，尤其是做近重复检测，不是完全无用。
embedding 相似度正是常用的内容比较手段，可以向量化。
内容信号在检测里也有位置，不只是服务推荐场景。
optionExplanations_en: Content is the signal most visible to attackers, who can simply rewrite copy or generate new text to dodge detection.
Content still helps as a secondary signal, especially for catching near-duplicates—it's not useless.
Embedding similarity is a standard way to compare content, so it can absolutely be vectorized.
Content signals have a role in detection too, not just in recommendation.

q: 比等下一次全量重训更快的做法是什么？
why: ANN 近邻索引能快速捕捉相似内容变体，把相似度当特征用，比完全依赖训练时见过的样本更敏捷。
why_en: Indexing bot-posted content separately in an ANN store lets the system flag semantically similar new posts by nearest-neighbor distance, without waiting for the next full retrain.
scenario: 平台发现一批 bot 正在发布语义近似的垃圾内容，需要快速响应新变体。
options: 把 bot 内容单独建 ANN 索引做特征
检测只能等待监督模型下一次重新训练
直接删除所有文本相关的特征信号
只做逐字完全一致的字符串匹配去重
whenOtherWins: 如果攻击主要不靠内容重复，而靠账号关系和节奏，图/行为特征会更有收益。
tradeoff: 近邻索引的实时响应 vs 完全依赖模型训练见过的样本

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻索引，能快速在向量空间里找到最相似的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index approximately finds the nearest vectors in an embedding space without scanning every item.

options_en: Index bot content separately in an ANN store as a feature.
Detection can only wait for the supervised model's next retrain cycle.
Directly drop every text-related feature signal.
Deduplicate using only exact, character-for-character string matching.
q_en: What responds faster than waiting for the next full retrain?
scenario_en: The platform sees bots posting semantically similar spam and needs to react to new variants quickly.
optionExplanations: 把 bot 内容单独建 ANN 近邻索引，新变体一出现就能按相似距离被捕捉成特征，不用等重训。
重训通常是天级/周级，跟不上新变体冒出来的速度。
删掉全部文本特征会丢掉近重复这类有效辅助信号。
bot 稍微改写文案就能绕过完全字符串匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Indexing bot content separately in an ANN store lets a new variant get caught by similarity distance the moment it appears, no retrain needed.
Retrains typically run daily or weekly, too slow to catch fresh variants.
Dropping all text features loses a useful secondary signal like near-duplicate detection.
A small rewrite is enough for a bot to slip past exact string matching.

scenario: bot 常成群批量互关、集中在少数 IP 上，你要从社交图里取能喂进下游模型的特征。
q: bot detection 可用的图/网络特征包括哪些？（多选）
why: 社交图暴露账号在网络中的角色和异常连接模式；图 embedding 能把多种关系压缩成下游模型可用的特征。
why_en: Follow ratios, connection growth speed, clustering coefficients, and graph embeddings all expose how an account's network position differs from a normal user's.
options: 粉丝/关注比例
连接增长速度
聚类系数
图 embedding
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Account[Account node] --> Follow[Follow ratio]
  Account --> Growth[Growth speed]
  Account --> Cluster[Cluster coefficient]
  Account --> Emb[Graph embedding]
  Emb --> Model[Bot model]
options_en: Follower-to-following ratio.
How fast new connections form.
Clustering coefficient.
Graph embedding.
q_en: Which graph or network features can bot detection use? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Bots tend to mass-follow each other from a handful of IPs, so you want graph features you can feed into the downstream model.
optionExplanations: 粉丝/关注比例明显偏斜，是常见的 bot 网络特征。
异常快的连接增长速度常是批量操作留下的痕迹。
星形关注农场会让聚类系数出现明显异常。
图 embedding 把账号在图中的角色压缩成向量，供下游模型使用。
optionExplanations_en: A clearly skewed follower-to-following ratio is a common bot network tell.
Unusually fast connection growth often signals bulk automated operations.
Star-shaped follow farms produce a visibly abnormal clustering coefficient.
Graph embeddings compress an account's network role into a vector the downstream model can use.

scenario: 大量低级 bot 是当天注册、无头像、手机未验证就开始批量关注，作案成本极低。
q: 账号元数据（注册时间、验证状态等）为什么仍然有价值？
why: 低级 bot 往往在注册、资料和登录模式上露出破绽；高级 bot 可以伪造这些字段，所以要和行为/图信号组合使用。
why_en: Account age, verification, device and login patterns, and profile completeness give useful baseline signals, especially for catching less sophisticated bots, but they must combine with behavior and graph signals since these fields can be faked.
options: 能提供账号年龄、验证状态等基线信号
元数据永远不会被伪造
元数据只用于账单结算
元数据单独就能解决所有 bot 类型
options_en: It gives baseline signals like account age and verification status.
Metadata can never be faked.
Metadata is only used for billing.
Metadata alone solves every type of bot.
q_en: Why are account metadata fields still useful?
scenario_en: Plenty of low-effort bots register the same day, skip the avatar and phone verification, and immediately mass-follow.
optionExplanations: 账号年龄、验证状态等元数据能提供基线信号，尤其对付低级 bot 有用，但要和行为/图信号组合。
高级 bot 也在学着伪造这些字段，谈不上永远可靠。
元数据是安全信号的一部分，不只是服务计费场景。
单靠元数据覆盖不了所有 bot 类型，需要组合其他信号。
optionExplanations_en: Fields like account age and verification status give useful baseline signals, especially against unsophisticated bots, but need to combine with behavior/graph signals.
Sophisticated bots are learning to fake these fields too, so it's far from unfakeable.
Metadata is part of the security signal set, not just a billing concern.
Metadata alone can't cover every bot type; it needs to combine with other signals.

q: 模型设计上应该怎么处理这种缺失？
why: 冷启动账号不能假装有正常历史；模型要显式学习「缺失」本身的含义，并用注册/设备/初始行为等可得信号顶上。
why_en: A brand-new account can't pretend to have a normal history, so the model needs explicit missing-value handling or a separate cold-start feature set built from signup and early activity.
scenario: 新账号刚注册，很多历史行为和网络特征缺失。
options: 显式支持缺失值，或使用新账号专用特征集
把缺失值当成 0 且不告诉模型发生了缺失
直接拒绝所有新账号
强制等待一周后再评分
whenOtherWins: 如果产品允许低风险冷却期，可先用限流收集信号再放开。
tradeoff: 为冷启动单独建模 vs 假装新账号也有完整历史
diagram:
flowchart LR
  New[New account] --> Missing[Missing history]
  New --> Signup[Signup device geo]
  Missing --> Mask[Missingness flags]
  Signup --> Cold[Cold-start features]
  Mask --> Model[Risk score]
  Cold --> Model
options_en: Explicitly support missing values, or use a dedicated cold-start feature set.
Treat missing values as zero without telling the model they're missing.
Reject every new account outright.
Force a one-week wait before scoring.
q_en: How should the model handle this missing history?
scenario_en: A newly registered account has little history, so many behavior and network features are missing.
optionExplanations: 让模型显式知道「缺失」本身是信号，或给新账号配专用特征集，这样冷启动账号也能拿到可解释的风险分。
把缺失伪装成正常的 0 会误导模型做出错误判断。
拒绝所有新账号会牺牲每一个真实新用户的体验。
固定等待一周只是拖延，没解决特征缺失本身的建模问题。
optionExplanations_en: Letting the model know missingness is itself a signal, or giving new accounts a dedicated feature set, still yields an explainable risk score at cold start.
Disguising missing values as a normal zero misleads the model into a wrong judgment.
Rejecting every new account sacrifices onboarding for every real new user.
A fixed one-week wait just delays things without solving the underlying missing-feature problem.

q: 最合适的起步模型是什么？
why: 轻量模型能分钟级训练、微秒级打分，适合当基线和线上 canary；它不是终点，但给后续复杂模型定了对照。
why_en: A logistic-regression baseline with simple frequency, device, and geo features trains in minutes, scores in microseconds, and doubles as a canary against regressions.
scenario: 你要先建立 bot detection benchmark，要求快、可解释、能作为 canary。
options: Logistic regression 加基础特征
用全量的多模态大模型逐条处理每一条内容
完全随机决定是否封禁，不看任何信号
只看用户昵称这一个字段做唯一判断依据
whenOtherWins: 如果已有强图/序列信号并且流量被过滤到小集合，重模型能带来更高召回。
tradeoff: 简单可解释的基线 vs 更强但更贵的复杂模型
options_en: Logistic regression with basic features.
Run a full-scale multimodal LLM over every single piece of content.
Decide bans completely at random, ignoring every signal.
Judge solely by the username field as the only basis for a decision.
q_en: What is the best starting model?
scenario_en: You need a first bot-detection benchmark that is fast, interpretable, and usable as a canary.
optionExplanations: logistic regression 加基础特征分钟级能训练、微秒级能打分，正好满足快、可解释、能当 canary 的要求。
训练和推理成本都远超「快、可解释」这个基线要求。
随机决策没有任何可解释性和判别力。
只看昵称这个弱字段，覆盖不了绝大多数真实 bot 模式。
optionExplanations_en: Logistic regression with basic features trains in minutes and scores in microseconds, exactly matching the fast, explainable, canary-ready bar.
Training and inference cost both far exceed what a fast, explainable baseline needs.
A random decision has zero explainability or discriminative power.
A single weak field like username covers nowhere near most real bot patterns.

scenario: 每天几十亿条内容，逐条跑多模态 LLM 的账单不可承受，而最强信号在账号行为里。
q: 为什么不该只用一个大型多模态 LLM 检查每条内容来做 bot detection？
why: bot 是账号行为问题，不只是内容理解问题；给每条内容跑大模型很贵，还会漏掉会话节奏、IP 切换、关注爆发这些强信号。
why_en: Bot detection is primarily about behavior and network structure, so running one giant content model on every post is expensive and still misses signals like session rhythm, IP swaps, and follow bursts.
options: bot detection 更依赖行为和图模式
LLM 完全没有能力读取任何形式的文本内容
LLM 天生就完全不能做任何分类任务
内容信号无论如何都比行为信号更强
tradeoff: 内容级大模型的语义理解 vs 行为/图模型对节奏和协同关系的覆盖
options_en: Bot detection relies more on behavior and graph patterns.
LLMs are completely incapable of reading any form of text content.
LLMs are inherently and completely incapable of classification tasks.
Content signals are always stronger than behavioral signals, no matter what.
q_en: Why not check every post with one large multimodal LLM?
scenario_en: With billions of posts a day, running a multimodal LLM on each one is unaffordable, and the strongest signal lives in account behavior.
optionExplanations: bot 更多是账号行为和社交图协同的问题，逐条帖子都跑大模型成本很高，还接不住时机和关系这类信号。
LLM 显然能读文本，这不是它在这里的短板。
分类只是接个输出头的问题，LLM 完全能做。
内容信号通常比行为/图信号更弱，这里说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Bot detection is mostly about account behavior and graph coordination, so per-post LLM calls are expensive and still miss signals like session rhythm, IP swaps, and follow bursts.
LLMs clearly can read text—that's not the weakness here.
Classification is just a matter of adding an output head; LLMs handle it fine.
Content signals are usually weaker than behavior/graph signals—this has it backwards.

q: 图分支为什么选 GraphSAGE？
why: GraphSAGE 学的是函数而不是查表，新节点可以在推理时直接用邻域和特征生成 embedding；邻居采样还能控制 fan-out 和延迟。
why_en: GraphSAGE is inductive, so it can embed brand-new nodes from their features and sampled neighborhoods at inference time instead of requiring retraining for every new account.
scenario: 需要识别新账号在社交图中的 botnet 关系，图持续增长。
options: 它是 inductive 的，能嵌入新节点
它只能处理训练时已经存在的固定节点
它不需要对邻居做任何采样
它比所有其他图模型都便宜
whenOtherWins: 如果图稳定且只做离线已知节点分析，node2vec 这类方法更简单。
tradeoff: 归纳式泛化到新节点 vs 只处理训练时已知节点

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种归纳式图神经网络，能给训练时没见过的新节点生成表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE is an inductive graph neural network that can embed new nodes it never saw during training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型学到的是一个函数，能泛化到新节点，而不是只记住训练图里的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inductive means the model learns a general function that works on new nodes instead of memorizing a fixed graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个节点连接的邻居数量，粉丝多的账号扇出会非常大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many neighbors a node has, so celebrity accounts have very large fan-out.

options_en: It is inductive, so it can embed new nodes directly.
It can only process the fixed set of nodes seen during training.
It requires no neighbor sampling at all.
It's cheaper than every other graph model, unconditionally.
q_en: Why choose GraphSAGE for the graph branch?
scenario_en: You need to detect botnet relationships for new accounts in a social graph that keeps growing.
optionExplanations: GraphSAGE 是归纳式的，能直接用新节点的特征和邻域现算 embedding，正好匹配图持续增长、新账号频出的场景。
这描述的是只能处理固定图方法的局限，GraphSAGE 不受此限。
邻居采样正是 GraphSAGE 控制 fan-out 和延迟的关键设计。
成本优劣要看图规模和替代方案，「比所有都便宜」是绝对化说法。
optionExplanations_en: GraphSAGE is inductive, so it can compute an embedding for a brand-new node straight from its features and sampled neighborhood—exactly what a constantly growing graph needs.
That describes the limitation of fixed-graph methods; GraphSAGE isn't bound by it.
Neighbor sampling is precisely how GraphSAGE controls fan-out and latency.
Cost depends on graph scale and the alternative, so 'cheaper than everything' is an overclaim.

scenario: 图分支默认只抓 2-hop 邻域；有人提议把邻域跳数改到 20-hop 看得更全。
q: 把邻域跳数从 2 大幅加深，对系统意味着什么？
why: 邻域规模随跳数迅速膨胀（尤其高粉丝账号），2-hop 已能看到局部协调关系；再加深收益递减但成本陡增。
why_en: Neighborhood size explodes with hop count, especially for high fan-out accounts, so a compact two-hop neighborhood already captures local coordination while deeper hops add cost with diminishing returns.
options: 计算和延迟会随跳数快速膨胀，收益却边际递减，通常不划算
跳数越深，成本只会呈线性增加，一直都很划算
跳数深浅完全不影响任何计算量或延迟
更深的跳数能自动让训练标签的数量变多
options_en: Compute and latency blow up with hop depth while returns diminish, so it's usually not worth it.
Cost only grows linearly with hop depth, so it stays a good trade at any depth.
Hop depth doesn't affect compute or latency in any way at all.
Deeper hops automatically produce a larger number of training labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图上距离账号 k 步以内能到达的节点集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-hop neighborhood is the set of nodes reachable within k edges of an account.

q_en: What does greatly increasing the graph-hop depth mean for the system?
scenario_en: The graph branch currently uses a 2-hop neighborhood; someone proposes 20 hops to see more context.
optionExplanations: 邻域规模随跳数指数级膨胀，粉丝多的账号尤其明显；两跳内就能看清本地的协同关系，再往深挖成本陡增但收获有限。
邻域规模是随跳数指数级膨胀，不是线性，这里低估了成本。
跳数越深要遍历的节点越多，计算量必然跟着涨。
跳数深浅只影响邻域大小，不会凭空生出新的训练标签。
optionExplanations_en: Neighborhood size explodes roughly exponentially with hop count, especially for high fan-out accounts; two hops already captures local coordination, and going deeper adds cost for shrinking returns.
Neighborhood size grows exponentially with hop depth, not linearly—this understates the cost.
Deeper hops always mean traversing more nodes, so compute necessarily rises.
Hop depth only changes neighborhood size; it can't manufacture new training labels out of nowhere.

q: 序列分支更合理的模型选择是什么？
why: GRU 能捕捉行为顺序和节奏，成本远低于 Transformer；这里建模的是事件序列的节奏，不是复杂自然语言语义。
why_en: A compact bidirectional GRU is enough to capture behavioral rhythm and order at a fraction of a Transformer's cost, since the task isn't about nuanced language understanding.
scenario: 要识别账号最近约 200 个事件的时间节奏，目标不是理解语言细节，计算也要省。
options: 小型双向 GRU/LSTM 类模型
超大规模文本 Transformer
只用平均发帖数这一个统计量
完全不建模事件的时间顺序
whenOtherWins: 如果需要捕捉很长距离复杂交互且候选很少，Transformer 序列模型可能赢。
tradeoff: 轻量 GRU 的低成本 vs Transformer 更强的长距离建模能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种轻量的循环神经网络，用来建模事件序列的先后顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GRU is a lightweight recurrent neural network used to model the order of a sequence of events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖自注意力机制处理序列，比 GRU 更贵但更擅长捕捉长距离依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer uses self-attention to process sequences and is more expensive than a GRU but better at capturing long-range dependencies.

options_en: A small bidirectional GRU/LSTM-style model.
A very large text Transformer.
Just a single statistic like average posts per day.
Skip modeling event order entirely.
q_en: What model is a better fit for the sequence branch?
scenario_en: You need to model the timing of roughly the last 200 account events, not language semantics, and compute is limited.
optionExplanations: 目标是约 200 个事件的节奏而不是语言语义，小型双向 GRU 计算便宜，也足以捕捉顺序和节奏。
为语言细节设计的重型 Transformer 在这里算力花得远超所需。
压成一个平均值会抹掉顺序和节奏里的绝大部分信息。
顺序正是本题要建模的对象，放弃顺序就丢了核心信号。
optionExplanations_en: The goal is timing cadence over roughly 200 events, not language semantics, so a small bidirectional GRU is cheap and still enough to capture order and rhythm.
A heavyweight Transformer built for language nuance spends far more compute than this task needs.
Collapsing everything into one average erases nearly all order and rhythm information.
Order is exactly what this task needs to model—dropping it throws away the core signal.

scenario: 要把一个账号几个月的点击/发帖事件流喂进模型，原始时间戳精确到毫秒且分布长尾。
q: 序列分支是怎么编码用户事件的？
why: 事件类型、离散化的时间间隔和先后顺序共同表达人类/机器节奏；五分钟这类时间桶能让模型学到可比较的模式。
why_en: The sequence branch embeds recent event types and bucketed timestamps in order before feeding them into the sequence model, preserving both timing and order.
options: 分桶时间戳，embedding 事件类型
把原始 JSON 直接拼接成字符串输入
把事件按字母顺序重新排序
只保留最后一个事件
options_en: Bucket timestamps and embed event types.
Concatenate raw JSON logs as a string input.
Re-sort events alphabetically.
Keep only the very last event.
q_en: How does the sequence branch encode user events?
scenario_en: You need to feed months of an account click and post events into the model, with raw millisecond timestamps and a long-tail distribution.
optionExplanations: 序列分支把时间戳分桶、事件类型做 embedding，再按发生顺序喂给模型，同时保留时机和顺序信息。
原始 JSON 既没归一化也没向量化，模型用不了。
按字母重排会打乱事件本来的时间顺序，节奏信息就没了。
只留最后一个事件等于丢掉了整个序列的意义。
optionExplanations_en: The sequence branch buckets timestamps, embeds event types, and feeds them in order, preserving both timing and sequence.
Raw JSON is neither normalized nor vectorized, so the model can't consume it directly.
Alphabetical resorting scrambles the actual time order, destroying rhythm information.
Keeping only the last event throws away the entire point of having a sequence.

scenario: 单看时间线的高频账号可能是真人运营号，单看图上的密集互关可能只是同校同学。
q: 图分支和序列分支融合（fusion）的目的是什么？
why: 交叉注意力能回答「这个节奏是否在同一图簇里重复出现」，让时间线和图关系互相校验，比单看一边更强。
why_en: Cross-attention fusion lets the behavioral timeline query the graph and vice versa, so the two views cross-check each other for coordinated bot patterns.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Seq[Behavior timeline] --> Fuse[Fusion]
  Graph[Graph footprint] --> Fuse
  Fuse --> Risk[Bot risk]
  Risk --> Action[Action policy]
options: 让账号的时间线和网络足迹互相校验
只是为了减少传输的 JSON 大小
替代所有人工标签
直接删除低风险账号

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一路表示去查询另一路表示，找到与自己相关的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-attention lets one sequence's representation query another sequence's representation for the parts relevant to it.

options_en: Let the account's timeline and network footprint cross-check each other.
Just to shrink the JSON payload size.
Replace the need for any human labels.
Directly delete low-risk accounts.
q_en: What is the purpose of fusing the graph and sequence branches?
scenario_en: A high-frequency timeline alone can be a real community manager, and a dense follow cluster alone can just be classmates.
optionExplanations: 交叉注意力让时间线表示去查询图表示、反过来也一样，两路信号互相校验，比单看一边更能发现协同 bot。
融合是表示层面的交互，不是数据传输优化。
融合只是产生更强的表示，产生不了标签，监督信号还得靠人工。
融合只输出风险分数，删账号是动作层的事，不是融合本身。
optionExplanations_en: Cross-attention lets the timeline representation query the graph representation and vice versa, so the two views cross-check each other and catch coordinated bots that either view alone would miss.
Fusion is a representation-level interaction, not a payload-size optimization.
Fusion produces a richer representation, not labels—supervision still comes from humans.
Fusion only outputs a risk score; deleting accounts is the action layer's job, not fusion's.

scenario: 图+序列双分支模型参数上亿，但每周只有几百条可信标签可用于监督训练。
q: 为什么 bot 主模型需要自监督预训练？
why: 标签少、模型较大，直接上二分类容易过拟合；先用自监督让图和序列分支学会平台的「语言」，监督阶段就更稳定。
why_en: With scarce labels and a fairly large model, jumping straight to supervised binary classification risks overfitting, so self-supervised pretraining lets each branch learn platform structure first.
options: 标签稀缺而模型较大，直接监督二分类容易过拟合
预训练能消除掉训练过程里的所有误判
预训练完全不需要用到任何真实数据
预训练只是为了单纯加速前端页面加载
options_en: Labels are scarce and the model is fairly large, so going straight to supervised classification risks overfitting.
Pretraining eliminates every single misclassification in the training process.
Pretraining needs no real data of any kind whatsoever.
Pretraining exists purely to speed up front-end page loading.
q_en: Why does the main bot model need self-supervised pretraining?
scenario_en: The graph-plus-sequence model has hundreds of millions of parameters, but only a few hundred trusted labels arrive each week.
optionExplanations: 标签少、模型又不小，直接上监督二分类容易过拟合；自监督预训练先让两个分支学会平台结构，监督阶段就更稳。
预训练不能保证零误判，只是让训练起点更好。
预训练同样要吃大量真实行为/图数据，不是无中生有。
预训练服务的是建模质量，跟前端页面性能无关。
optionExplanations_en: With scarce labels and a fairly large model, going straight to supervised binary classification risks overfitting; self-supervised pretraining lets both branches learn platform structure first, stabilizing the supervised stage.
Pretraining can't guarantee zero misclassification, it just gives training a better starting point.
Pretraining still consumes plenty of real behavior/graph data—it isn't free of data.
Pretraining serves modeling quality, unrelated to front-end page speed.

scenario: 预训练阶段不能碰调查员标签（要留作评估），手上只有海量无标签的图和事件流。
q: bot 主模型的自监督预训练任务包括哪些？（多选）
why: 这些任务让模型在没有标签的情况下学会正常社交图结构和行为「语言」；测试集标签必须留到评估阶段。
why_en: Masking graph attributes, predicting masked or next events, and contrasting same-user session clips all teach the model normal structure and rhythm without using any test labels.
options: 图侧遮蔽节点属性/丢边/辨别真假邻居
序列侧 masked event 和 next-event prediction
把同一用户的会话片段拉近，不同用户的片段推开
直接用测试集标签做监督训练
options_en: On the graph side: masking node attributes, dropping edges, and telling real neighbors from fake ones.
On the sequence side: masked-event and next-event prediction.
Contrastive learning: pull same-user session clips together, push different users' clips apart.
Train directly on the test-set labels.
q_en: Which self-supervised pretraining tasks fit the main bot model? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Pretraining cannot touch investigator labels, which are reserved for evaluation, so all you have is unlabeled graph and event data.
optionExplanations: 图侧靠遮蔽属性、丢边、辨别真假邻居这些自监督任务学正常图结构。
序列侧用掩码预测和下一事件预测学正常的行为节奏。
对比学习把同用户片段拉近、不同用户片段推远，学出账号级别的一致性表示。
测试集标签绝不能用于训练，否则评估会失去意义。
optionExplanations_en: On the graph side, masking attributes, dropping edges, and telling real neighbors from fake ones teaches normal graph structure self-supervised.
On the sequence side, masked-event and next-event prediction teaches normal behavioral rhythm.
Contrastive learning pulls same-user clips together and pushes different users' clips apart, learning an account-consistent representation.
Test-set labels must never be used for training, or the evaluation becomes meaningless.

scenario: 一个 bot 骚扰了 10 万用户，另一个只发了 3 条帖，业务目标是降低实际伤害。
q: bot 检测主模型的监督 loss 如何对齐「影响」这个目标？
why: 高影响 bot 更重要，所以按潜在受影响用户数加权；权重要设上限，避免单个爆款 spam 让梯度失控。
why_en: The loss is a weighted binary cross-entropy that emphasizes high-impact bot accounts, with weights capped so one viral spam post can't destabilize training.
options: 加权二元交叉熵，按影响力加权并设上限
只优化未加权的 accuracy
只优化生成文本的长度
只优化图节点的度数

termDefinitions.term: weighted binary cross-entropy / 加权二元交叉熵
termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个训练样本按重要性加权的二分类损失函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weighted binary cross-entropy is a binary classification loss that scales each example's contribution by an importance weight.

options_en: Weighted binary cross-entropy, weighted by impact and capped.
Optimize only unweighted accuracy.
Optimize only the length of generated text.
Optimize only the degree of a graph node.
q_en: How should the supervised loss align with user impact?
scenario_en: One bot reached 100k users while another posted three times, and the business goal is reducing actual harm.
optionExplanations: 用按潜在受影响用户数加权的二元交叉熵，并给权重设上限，让高影响 bot 更重要又不会让单个爆款样本主导梯度。
accuracy 反映不出谁受到了伤害，退回它就丢了「影响」这个目标。
文本长度和分类目标完全无关。
节点度数只是一个特征，不是训练要优化的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Weighting binary cross-entropy by potential affected-user count, with a cap, makes high-impact bots matter more without letting one viral sample dominate the gradient.
Accuracy doesn't reflect who got hurt, so falling back to it drops the 'impact' objective.
Text length has nothing to do with the classification target.
Node degree is a feature, not something the training loss should optimize.

q: 这段伪代码体现了什么设计？
why: 它把潜在伤害（受影响用户数）纳入训练目标提升召回，但 cap 防止单个爆款 spam 主导梯度。
why_en: The code shows impact-weighted binary cross-entropy where the weight is capped, so high-exposure accounts matter more without letting one viral post destabilize the gradient.
scenario: 你要解释 bot loss 如何重视高影响账号但避免梯度失控。
codeSample:
weight = min(users_exposed, cap)
loss = weight * BCE(label, bot_score)
options: 影响加权 BCE，并对权重做截断（cap）
无监督聚类损失
Platt scaling 校准
ANN 近邻检索
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求每个账号同等处理而不按影响优先，未加权或公平约束 loss 更合适。
tradeoff: 按影响力加权提升高危账号召回 vs 截断权重换取梯度稳定

termDefinitions.meaning: 给样本权重设的最大值，防止极端样本主导训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cap is a maximum value on a sample's weight so one extreme example can't dominate training.

options_en: Impact-weighted BCE with the weight capped.
An unsupervised clustering loss.
Platt-scaling calibration.
ANN nearest-neighbor retrieval.
q_en: What design does this pseudocode express?
scenario_en: You need to explain how the bot loss emphasizes high-impact accounts without letting gradients blow up.
optionExplanations: `weight = min(users_exposed, cap)` 再乘 BCE，正是按受影响用户数加权、同时截断权重防止梯度失控的设计。
代码里没有任何聚类相关操作。
Platt scaling 是训练后校准分数的方法，不是这里的训练损失。
ANN 检索是找相似内容，不是损失函数。
optionExplanations_en: `weight = min(users_exposed, cap)` times BCE is exactly weighting by affected-user count while capping the weight to keep gradients stable.
There's no clustering operation anywhere in this code.
Platt scaling calibrates scores after training; it isn't the training loss shown here.
ANN retrieval finds similar content—it isn't a loss function.

q: 最重要的 serving 结构设计是什么？
why: 级联能把重模型调用量降到可控范围，轻模型的阈值还是个可调参数，能在资源和效果之间权衡。
why_en: A two-stage cascade reserves the expensive graph-sequence model for accounts that pass a cheap first-stage filter, keeping GPU cost bounded at billions of daily actions.
scenario: 每天有数十亿动作，重图序列模型需要 GPU。
options: 两阶段级联：轻模型过滤，重模型查可疑
每个动作都跑一遍全量重模型
只做离线的年度评分
取消所有缓存以简化架构
whenOtherWins: 如果流量很小或每次决策风险极高，直接跑重模型也可能合理。
tradeoff: 级联降低重模型调用量 vs 轻模型阈值可能漏掉部分可疑账号
diagram:
flowchart LR
  All[All accounts] --> Light[Light filter]
  Light --> Clear[Mostly normal]
  Light --> Suspicious[Suspicious]
  Suspicious --> Heavy[Graph sequence model]
  Heavy --> Action[Calibrated action]
options_en: A two-stage cascade: light model filters, heavy model checks suspects.
Run the full heavy model on every single action.
Only do offline scoring once a year.
Remove all caching to simplify the architecture.
q_en: What is the most important serving-architecture choice?
scenario_en: The platform has billions of daily actions, and the heavy graph-sequence model needs GPUs.
optionExplanations: 两阶段级联用便宜的轻模型先过滤，把重图序列模型的预算集中在可疑账号上，能把 GPU 调用量控制在可承受范围。
数十亿动作全跑重模型，GPU 成本不可持续。
年度批处理完全跟不上风险变化的速度。
取消缓存只会让邻域和序列编码反复重算，成本更高。
optionExplanations_en: A cheap first stage filters traffic, concentrating the expensive graph-sequence model's budget on suspicious accounts, keeping GPU cost within a sustainable range.
Running the heavy model on every one of billions of daily actions is an unsustainable GPU cost.
A once-a-year offline batch can't keep up with how fast risk changes.
Dropping caching just forces repeated recomputation of neighborhood and sequence encodings, raising cost.

scenario: 重模型每次推理要拉整个图邻域，500M 账号全量跑不现实，得先筛掉明显正常的账号。
q: 轻量过滤模型如何与重模型的判断对齐？
why: 轻模型的目标不是独立最优，而是找出重模型可能打高分的账号；teacher/student 训练能省计算又少漏可疑样本。
why_en: The lightweight filter is trained in a teacher/student fashion to approximate the heavy model's score, which preserves recall while cutting the number of accounts sent to the expensive model.
options: 用 teacher/student 训练轻模型近似
让轻模型随机输出没有依据的分数结果
只在前端点击数据这一类信号上单独训练轻模型
轻模型完全不使用任何形式的监督标签

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个大模型的输出去训练一个更小的模型来近似它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Teacher/student training trains a small model to approximate the outputs of a larger one.

options_en: Train the light model as a student to approximate the teacher.
Have the light model output ungrounded, random score results.
Train the light model solely on this kind of front-end click signal alone.
The light model uses no form of supervised label whatsoever.
q_en: How should the lightweight filter align with the heavy model?
scenario_en: The heavy model pulls a whole graph neighborhood per call, so scoring all 500M accounts is impossible without a cheap prefilter.
optionExplanations: 用师生蒸馏训练轻模型去近似重模型的判断，能省计算又不太漏掉重模型会打高分的账号。
随机分数没法近似重模型的判断。
前端点击数据和 bot 风险判断没有对齐关系。
没有对齐目标，轻模型就学不到该逼近谁。
optionExplanations_en: Training the light model teacher/student style to approximate the heavy model's judgment saves compute while preserving recall on what the heavy model would flag.
Random scores can't approximate the heavy model's judgment at all.
Front-end click data has no alignment with bot-risk judgment.
Without an alignment target, the light model has nothing to learn to approximate.

scenario: 重模型 GPU 账单超预算，但多数账号的图邻域和活动序列在一天内几乎不变。
q: bot 检测重模型可用哪些推理优化？（多选）
why: 量化和缓存都能降低成本，但必须配合质量回归测试，尤其在图邻域没有明显变化时缓存最有效。
why_en: Quantization-aware training and caching graph or sequence encoders both cut serving cost, but they must be paired with quality regression testing.
options: quantization-aware training
缓存图 embedding
缓存活动序列编码
完全放弃模型质量评估

termDefinitions.term: quantization-aware training / 量化感知训练
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时就模拟低精度数值，让部署后用更少内存也能保持效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization-aware training simulates low-precision math during training so the deployed model stays accurate with less memory.

options_en: Quantization-aware training.
Caching graph embeddings.
Caching activity-sequence encodings.
Dropping model quality evaluation entirely.
q_en: Which inference optimizations can the heavy bot model use? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The heavy model blows the GPU budget, yet for most accounts the graph neighborhood and activity sequence barely change within a day.
optionExplanations: 训练时模拟低精度数值，部署后能用更少内存保持效果。
图邻域没大变化时，缓存图 embedding 能省下重复计算。
活动模式没大变化时，缓存序列编码同样能省计算。
推理优化必须配合质量回归测试，放弃评估会让人看不见质量退化。
optionExplanations_en: Simulating low-precision math during training keeps accuracy while using less memory at deployment.
When a graph neighborhood hasn't changed much, caching its embedding skips recomputation.
When activity patterns haven't changed much, caching the sequence encoding likewise skips recomputation.
Inference optimizations must pair with quality regression testing—dropping evaluation hides quality regressions.

scenario: 全量每天重算 500M 账号太贵，只想在账号风险可能真的变化时才重新打分。
q: 哪些事件适合触发 bot 风险重新评估？（多选）
why: 按事件触发重新评估比每个动作都全量重跑更省计算，也能在风险变化时更及时响应。
why_en: Re-scoring on registration, suspicious activity thresholds, joining a known bot cluster, or user reports is far cheaper than re-running every account on every action.
options: 账号注册
批量关注/快速发帖等活动阈值
加入已知的 bot 网络簇
收到用户举报
options_en: Account registration.
Crossing an activity threshold like bulk follows or rapid posting.
Joining a known bot cluster.
Receiving a user report.
q_en: Which events should trigger bot-risk reassessment? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Rescoring all 500M accounts daily is too expensive, so you only want to re-evaluate when an account risk plausibly changed.
optionExplanations: 新账号一出现就该先用元数据/早期行为打一次初始分。
越过批量关注、快速发帖这类活动阈值是典型的再评估触发点。
加入已知 bot 簇是很强的图协同信号，值得立刻重新评估。
用户举报应该优先触发重新评估。
optionExplanations_en: A brand-new account should get an initial score right away from metadata and early activity.
Crossing an activity threshold like bulk follows or rapid posting is a classic re-scoring trigger.
Joining a known bot cluster is a strong graph-coordination signal worth an immediate re-check.
A user report should trigger priority re-evaluation.

q: 这会带来什么风险？
why: 被及时拦截的正例缺少后续行为，模型可能学到「有完整行为数据=正常」，需要 holdout 或反事实样本来补足。
why_en: Because effective interception removes bots before they accumulate a full behavioral history, the model risks learning that having lots of history means legitimate.
scenario: 系统很快就拦截 bot，导致训练数据里高风险账号缺少后续完整行为。
options: 误学「有历史即正常」
模型判断会自动变得更公平
线上推理延迟会自动降低
训练标签会自动变成无偏
whenOtherWins: 如果模型只观察拦截前特征并严格按同一时间点训练，风险会小一些。
tradeoff: 越早拦截 bot（降低伤害）vs 训练数据里正例行为历史越不完整
options_en: Mislearning that having a history means legitimate.
Model judgments automatically become fairer.
Online inference latency automatically drops.
Training labels automatically become unbiased.
q_en: What risk does this create?
scenario_en: Fast interception means high-risk bot accounts often lack complete later behavior in the training logs.
optionExplanations: 被及时拦截的 bot 缺少后续行为，模型可能把「行为历史完整」错误地学成「正常」的信号。
这里的风险是标签偏差，跟公平性没有直接关系。
标签偏差和推理延迟是两回事，快速拦截不会自动改善延迟。
标签依然是有偏的，需要靠额外留一部分账号不处理来获取对照数据，或者构造反事实样本来补齐。
optionExplanations_en: Bots caught quickly never accumulate later behavior, so the model can mistakenly learn that having a full history equals legitimate.
The risk here is label bias, not fairness—the two aren't directly linked.
Label bias and inference latency are unrelated; fast interception doesn't automatically improve latency.
The labels stay biased and need dedicated fixes like holdouts or counterfactual samples.

q: 这类 holdout 的关键约束是什么？
why: holdout 能提供反事实数据，也能让攻击者更难反推检测逻辑，但绝不能造成明显用户伤害，需要小比例和严格风险控制。
why_en: Holdouts collect valuable counterfactual bot behavior and make detection logic harder to reverse-engineer, but they must stay small and tightly risk-controlled so bots aren't given free rein.
scenario: 为收集 bot 完整行为并隐藏检测规则，你考虑对少量疑似 bot 暂不立即处理。
options: 严格控制风险和流量，避免被攻击者反向利用
让所有被怀疑的 bot 都直接放行不管
完全不记录任何相关的操作日志
只把它用于前端的 A/B 实验场景
whenOtherWins: 如果风险极高（如恶意链接传播），软动作或沙盒比完全放行更合适。
tradeoff: 保留 holdout 换取反事实数据和隐藏检测逻辑 vs 放任 bot 造成的伤害规模
options_en: Tightly control risk and volume to avoid attackers exploiting it.
Let every suspected bot straight through with no oversight at all.
Keep absolutely no logs of any related activity.
Use it only for a front-end A/B experiment scenario.
q_en: What is the key constraint for this kind of holdout?
scenario_en: To collect complete bot behavior and hide detection logic, you consider delaying action on a tiny set of suspected bots.
optionExplanations: 把 holdout 限定在小比例、严格风险控制内，既能拿到反事实行为数据，又不会被攻击者规模化利用。
holdout 是小比例受控延迟，不是对所有 bot 全面放行。
日志记录正是 holdout 的价值所在，不留痕就白做了。
把用途限定在前端实验会错失收集完整 bot 行为这个核心目的。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the holdout small and tightly risk-controlled yields counterfactual behavior data without letting attackers exploit it at scale.
A holdout is a small, controlled delay, not a blanket pass-through for every bot.
Logging is exactly where a holdout's value comes from—no trace means wasted effort.
Limiting it to front-end experiments misses the whole point of collecting full bot behavior.

q: 在线评估应该怎么采样？
why: 边界和模型分歧处的样本信息量最大；低 prevalence 下纯随机标注效率太低，重加权能把这些样本还原成总体估计。
why_en: Online evaluation should use importance sampling weighted toward boundary and disagreement cases, then reweight, because with prevalence under 1% pure random sampling would need an enormous sample size.
scenario: 候选模型和旧模型标出的账号不同，bot prevalence 很低，人工标签很贵。
options: 按分数和分歧点采样，再重加权
均匀随机抽取少量样本且不重加权
只标最高分的账号并当成总体估计
完全不做人工验证
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是估计全站无条件 prevalence，仍需保留一部分随机样本。
tradeoff: 把标注预算集中在高信息量样本 vs 均匀随机采样的简单无偏性
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Scores[Model scores] --> Sample[Sample by score and disagreement]
  Sample --> Human[Investigator labels]
  Human --> Reweight[Reweight estimates]
  Reweight --> Metrics[Online metrics]

termDefinitions.meaning: 按信息量而非均匀概率抽样，再用权重修正估计结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Importance sampling draws samples in proportion to how informative they are, then reweights the results to correct for that bias.

options_en: Sample by score and disagreement, then reweight.
Sample a small number uniformly at random without reweighting.
Label only the highest-scoring accounts and treat that as the population.
Skip manual verification altogether.
q_en: How should online evaluation sample accounts?
scenario_en: The candidate and old models flag different accounts, bot prevalence is low, and human labels are expensive.
optionExplanations: 按模型分数和两模型分歧点采样再重加权，能把标注预算集中在信息量最高的账号上，还原成无偏的总体估计。
prevalence 低于 1% 时，均匀随机抽样需要巨大样本量才够稳定。
只看高分子集外推整体会系统性高估检出率，忽略假阴性。
不做人工验证就没法判断候选模型是否真的更好。
optionExplanations_en: Sampling by score and model disagreement, then reweighting, concentrates the label budget on the most informative accounts while still recovering an unbiased population estimate.
With prevalence under 1%, uniform random sampling needs a huge sample size to be stable.
Extrapolating from only the top-scoring subset systematically overestimates detection, ignoring false negatives.
Skipping manual verification leaves no way to tell whether the candidate model is actually better.

scenario: 上线评审要一个既能给产品也能给法务交代的线上指标，误封真实用户是硬红线。
q: bot detection 的主要在线业务指标可以概括为什么？
why: 这个指标直接衡量真实用户感受到的 bot 骚扰，并把误伤设成硬 guardrail，比抽象的模型分数更贴近业务目标。
why_en: The primary online metric is the reduction in bot interactions per legitimate user, subject to keeping the false-positive rate on account restrictions under 1%.
options: bot 互动量下降，且误伤率 <1%
模型 accuracy 达到最大
GPU 利用率达到最大
封禁账号数量达到最大

termDefinitions.meaning: 设定的硬性上限指标，防止优化方向跑偏、牺牲用户体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a hard limit that keeps optimization from drifting into an outcome that harms users.

options_en: Bot interactions per user drop, with false positives under 1%.
Maximum model accuracy.
Maximum GPU utilization.
The maximum number of banned accounts.
q_en: How can the main online business metric for bot detection be summarized?
scenario_en: The launch review needs one online metric that satisfies both product and legal, and wrongly banning real users is a hard red line.
optionExplanations: 把主指标定成真实用户感受到的 bot 互动量下降，同时给误伤率设 <1% 的硬护栏，比抽象分数更贴近业务目标。
accuracy 在类别不平衡下会失真，代表不了体验。
GPU 利用率是成本指标，不是用户体验指标。
只追封禁数量会激励系统宁可错杀。
optionExplanations_en: Setting the primary metric as the drop in bot interactions users actually feel, with a hard guardrail of under 1% false positives, tracks the business goal far better than an abstract score.
Accuracy gets distorted under class imbalance and doesn't represent user experience.
GPU utilization is a cost metric, not an experience metric.
Chasing raw ban counts rewards over-banning.

scenario: 人工标签一周才回来几百条，但 A/B 实验必须在几天内看出这版模型有没有变好。
q: bot detection 在线可以用哪些 proxy metric 快速迭代？（多选）
why: 这些信号能比人工标签更快反映用户体验和误伤情况，但都带噪声，应该和人工标签结合使用。
why_en: User reports, appeal success rates, and network interaction rates all give faster feedback than manual labels, though they're noisier and should be combined with investigator labels.
options: bot/spam/fake account 举报量
申诉成功率
好友请求接受率/消息回复率
代码提交行数
options_en: Volume of bot/spam/fake-account reports.
Appeal success rate.
Friend-request acceptance rate / message response rate.
Lines of code committed.
q_en: Which proxy metrics can speed up online iteration? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: Human labels trickle in a few hundred a week, but the A/B test has to show whether this model version helped within days.
optionExplanations: 举报量是用户主动发出的信号，量大但带噪声，能快速反映体感变化。
申诉成功率能反映有多少误伤账号被纠正回来。
好友请求接受率和消息回复率反映真实用户对互动的接受程度，是网络健康度信号。
代码提交行数是工程活动指标，和检测效果毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Report volume is a user-initiated, noisy but high-volume signal that reflects experience shifts quickly.
Appeal success rate reflects how many wrongly flagged accounts get corrected.
Friend-request acceptance and message response rates reflect how willing real users are to interact—a network-health signal.
Lines of code committed is an engineering-activity metric with no bearing on detection quality.

scenario: 封禁阈值定在 recall 90% 那个操作点，离线评估要能预测上线后的真实表现。
q: bot detection 的离线评估应该包括哪些指标？（多选）
why: 离线指标既要看整体判别力（PR-AUC），也要看动作阈值处的精确率、影响加权效果和多早能抓到 bot。
why_en: Offline evaluation should include an operating-point metric like Precision@Recall90, overall PR-AUC, impact-weighted quality, and how early bots get caught.
options: Precision@Recall90 或类似操作点指标
PR-AUC
impact-weighted 指标
early detection rate

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下的面积，类别不平衡时比 ROC-AUC 更能反映效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PR-AUC is the area under the precision-recall curve and is more informative than ROC-AUC when classes are imbalanced.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把召回率固定在 90% 时衡量精确率的操作点指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision at Recall 90 measures precision at the operating point where recall is fixed at ninety percent.

options_en: Precision@Recall90 or a similar operating-point metric.
PR-AUC.
Impact-weighted metrics.
Early detection rate.
q_en: Which offline metrics should bot-detection evaluation include? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The ban threshold sits at the 90%-recall operating point, and offline evaluation has to predict what happens in production.
optionExplanations: Precision@Recall90 这类操作点指标对齐了自动化动作实际用的阈值。
PR-AUC 衡量整体判别力，类别不平衡下比 ROC-AUC 更稳健。
impact-weighted 指标按潜在受影响用户数加权，对齐「减少伤害」这个业务目标。
early detection rate 衡量多快能在行为早期抓到 bot，抓得越早累积伤害越小。
optionExplanations_en: Precision@Recall90-style operating-point metrics align with the threshold automated actions actually use.
PR-AUC measures overall discriminative power and is more robust than ROC-AUC under class imbalance.
Impact-weighted metrics weigh quality by potential affected-user count, aligning with the 'reduce harm' business goal.
Early detection rate measures how soon bots get caught—the earlier, the less cumulative harm.

q: 验证集应该如何设计？
why: 对抗漂移意味着未来 bot 和过去不同；按时间分层留出未来行为，能让验证集更接近线上真实会遇到的新策略。
why_en: Because adversarial drift means future bot behavior differs from the past, time-stratified validation holds out future behavior so the test set better reflects unseen attack patterns.
scenario: bot 攻击策略随时间变化，你担心验证集过于容易。
options: 按时间分层，留出未来行为测试未见过的攻击模式
把所有时间点随机打散后再混合切分
只用最早期、最陈旧的历史样本做验证
只看训练集本身的效果，不做验证
whenOtherWins: 如果只验证稳定的元数据 pipeline，随机抽样也可作为辅助。
tradeoff: 按时间切分更贴近真实漂移 vs 随机切分的方差更小、更容易
options_en: Time-stratify and hold out future behavior to test unseen attack patterns.
Randomly shuffle every timestamp together before splitting.
Validate only on the oldest, most dated historical samples.
Only look at performance on the training set itself, skip validation.
q_en: How should the validation set be designed?
scenario_en: Bot attack strategies change over time, and you are worried the validation set is too easy.
optionExplanations: 按时间分层把未来的行为留出来做验证，能让测试集更贴近线上真正会遇到的新攻击策略。
随机切分会让模型「偷看」未来模式，验证结果会过于乐观。
最早期样本代表不了对抗漂移后的新策略。
训练集上的表现说明不了模型的泛化能力。
optionExplanations_en: Time-stratifying and holding out future behavior makes the test set closer to the new attack strategies actually seen online.
Random splitting lets the model peek at future patterns, making validation results overly optimistic.
The earliest historical samples can't represent strategies that emerged after adversarial drift.
Training-set performance says nothing about generalization.

scenario: 新旧两个模型版本都输出 0.6 分，但切换后封禁阈值必须保持同样的误伤率。
q: bot 模型为什么需要做 calibration？
why: 0.6 分不一定代表 60% 是 bot；校准把分数映射成更可信的概率，动作阈值和模型版本切换才能稳定。
why_en: A raw score of 0.6 doesn't mean a 60% chance of being a bot, so calibration maps scores to trustworthy probabilities and keeps action thresholds stable across model versions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw score] --> Cal[Calibration]
  Cal --> Prob[Usable probability]
  Prob --> T1[Demote threshold]
  Prob --> T2[Ban threshold]
  Prob --> Monitor[Version comparison]
options: 原始分数不等于真实概率，需要校准才可信
校准能让模型永远不出错
校准只适用于生成式 AI 模型
校准会自动消除所有误伤
options_en: Raw scores are not true probabilities, so they need calibration.
Calibration guarantees the model is never wrong.
Calibration applies only to generative AI models.
Calibration automatically eliminates all false positives.
q_en: Why does a bot model need calibration?
scenario_en: Old and new model versions both output 0.6, yet after the swap the ban threshold has to keep the same false-positive rate.
optionExplanations: 模型给出的 0.6 分不代表 60% 的真实概率，校准是把分数变成可信数值，这样封禁/降权的界线换模型版本也不会跳变。
校准只是让分数更可信，不改变模型本身的判别力，消不了错误。
校准适用于任何输出分数的分类器，不限生成式模型。
校准不改变判别能力本身，也就消除不了误伤。
optionExplanations_en: A raw score of 0.6 doesn't mean a 60% chance of being a bot; calibration maps scores into trustworthy probabilities so action thresholds stay stable across model versions.
Calibration only makes scores more trustworthy—it doesn't change the model's underlying discriminative power or errors.
Calibration applies to any score-producing classifier, not just generative models.
Calibration doesn't change discriminative power, so it can't eliminate false positives either.

scenario: 验证集只有几千条可信标签，要把模型原始风险分映射成可直接比较的真实概率。
q: bot 模型常用的校准方法包括哪些？（多选）
why: 直方分箱简单直接，isotonic 更灵活但需要更多数据，Platt scaling 用两参数 sigmoid，对少量关键点更实用。
why_en: Histogram binning, isotonic regression, and Platt scaling are the three calibration approaches discussed, trading off simplicity against data requirements.
options: histogram binning
isotonic regression
Platt scaling
数据库分片（sharding）

termDefinitions.term: histogram binning / 直方分箱校准
termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测概率分到等宽区间，用每个区间的真实命中率做校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Histogram binning buckets predicted scores into equal-width bins and calibrates using each bin's observed accuracy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 学习一个单调的分段常数映射，不假设固定函数形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isotonic regression learns a monotonic step-wise mapping without assuming a fixed function shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个两参数的 sigmoid 函数把原始分数映射为概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling fits a two-parameter sigmoid function to map raw scores into probabilities.

options_en: Histogram binning.
Isotonic regression.
Platt scaling.
Database sharding.
q_en: Which calibration methods are commonly used for bot models? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: The validation set holds only a few thousand trusted labels, and raw risk scores must become comparable real probabilities.
optionExplanations: 把预测分数分到等宽区间，用每个区间的真实命中率做校准，简单直接。
学一个单调分段常数映射，比固定函数形式更灵活，但需要更多数据。
用两参数 sigmoid 拟合分数到概率，标签少也能用。
分片是数据库扩容手段，和分数校准毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Bucketing scores into equal-width bins and calibrating by each bin's observed hit rate is simple and direct.
Learning a monotonic step-wise mapping is more flexible than a fixed function shape, but needs more data.
Fitting a two-parameter sigmoid works even with few labels.
Sharding is a database-scaling technique, unrelated to score calibration.

q: 更适合的简单校准方法是什么？
why: Platt scaling 只拟合两个 sigmoid 参数，在人工标签有限、只关心几个关键阈值时比 isotonic 更容易落地。
why_en: Platt scaling is attractive with limited labels because it fits just two sigmoid parameters on a small holdout set, unlike more data-hungry methods like isotonic regression.
scenario: 人工标签很少，只关心少数几个动作阈值附近的校准精度。
options: Platt scaling
另外训练一个超大模型专门做校准
完全不做校准
只看模型输出的最大分数
whenOtherWins: 如果有大量校准数据且分数-概率关系很不规则，isotonic 可能更准。
tradeoff: Platt scaling 的少参数、易落地 vs isotonic 在数据充足时更灵活
options_en: Platt scaling.
Train an entirely separate huge model just for calibration.
Skip calibration entirely.
Just look at the maximum score the model outputs.
q_en: What simple calibration method is a better fit here?
scenario_en: Human labels are scarce, and you only care about calibration near a few action thresholds.
optionExplanations: 这套校准方法只有两个自由参数（一条 sigmoid 曲线），标签少、只盯几个动作阈值时，落地明显比 isotonic 轻松。
标签量根本撑不起再训练一个大模型。
不校准会让误伤率 <1% 这类 guardrail 失去意义。
只看最大分数解决不了把分数映射成概率这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: This method fits just two free parameters on one sigmoid curve, so with scarce labels and only a few thresholds to watch, it lands far more easily than isotonic regression.
The label volume can't support training an entirely separate large model.
Skipping calibration makes a guardrail like 'false positives under 1%' meaningless.
Looking only at the max score doesn't solve the score-to-probability mapping problem.

scenario: 监督模型对已知 bot 家族 precision 很高，但新脚本模式要几周才被标注覆盖。
q: 异常检测在 bot 系统中主要起什么作用？
why: 攻击者不断制造新模式，异常检测能提出可疑账号供调查和扩充训练集，但要结合业务影响，而不是抓所有「怪」账号。
why_en: Anomaly detection helps surface new bot patterns that supervised labels haven't covered yet, feeding investigation and future training data.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Features[Behavior graph features] --> Anom[Anomaly detector]
  Anom --> Queue[Review queue]
  Queue --> Human[Investigator]
  Human --> Labels[New labels]
  Labels --> Train[Supervised update]
options: 发现未被监督标签覆盖的新型 bot 模式
完全替代所有监督模型
保证系统不再需要任何人工审核
只用于数据可视化展示
options_en: Surfacing new bot patterns not yet covered by supervised labels.
Fully replacing every supervised model.
Guaranteeing the system never needs manual review again.
Serving only as a data-visualization tool.
q_en: What role does anomaly detection mainly play in the bot system?
scenario_en: The supervised model has high precision on known bot families, but new script patterns take weeks to reach the label set.
optionExplanations: 异常检测的定位是发现监督标签还没覆盖到的新型 bot 模式，把可疑账号送进调查队列扩充训练集。
异常检测的结果仍要靠调查/监督验证，替代不了监督模型。
异常线索仍需人工确认，消除不了人工审核的需求。
异常检测服务于发现新模式，不只是拿来做可视化。
optionExplanations_en: Anomaly detection's job is surfacing new bot patterns supervised labels haven't covered yet, feeding suspicious accounts into the investigation queue to grow training data.
Anomaly output still needs investigation and supervised verification—it can't replace supervised models.
Anomaly leads still require human confirmation, so manual review doesn't go away.
Anomaly detection is for finding new patterns, not just a visualization tool.

scenario: 完全没有标签，只有 500M 账号的高维行为特征，需要一个便宜的方法先挑出可疑账号。
q: isolation forest 识别异常的核心直觉是什么？
why: 多棵随机树里，越少切分就能被孤立的点越异常；这是无监督方法，不需要标签，计算效率也较高。
why_en: Isolation forests score anomalies by how quickly random feature splits isolate a point, since anomalies are rare and different from the bulk of the data.
options: 异常点少且不同，更容易被快速孤立
异常点总是聚集在特征均值附近
必须先有标签才能训练
它只能处理文本类特征

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多棵随机切分树，越容易被孤立的点越可能是异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation forest randomly splits the feature space with many trees, and points that get isolated in fewer splits are scored as more anomalous.

options_en: Anomalies are rare and different, so they get isolated faster.
Anomalies always cluster near the feature mean.
It must have labels before it can be trained.
It can only handle text-type features.
q_en: What is the core intuition behind isolation forest anomaly detection?
scenario_en: With no labels at all, just high-dimensional behavior features for 500M accounts, you need a cheap way to surface suspects.
optionExplanations: 异常点数量少、和大多数样本不同，随机切分树只需要更少的切分次数就能把它孤立出来。
异常点通常远离大多数数据，不是靠近均值聚集。
它是无监督方法，不需要标签就能训练。
它适用于任意数值/类别特征，不限于文本。
optionExplanations_en: Anomalies are rare and different from the bulk of the data, so random split trees need fewer cuts to isolate them.
Anomalies are usually far from the bulk of the data, not clustered near the mean.
It's unsupervised—no labels are needed to train it.
It works on any numeric or categorical feature, not just text.

q: 更适合先用的方法是什么？
why: isolation forest 对高维表格异常计算高效，不需要强分布假设，适合作为第一道筛查。
why_en: Isolation forests are efficient first-pass detectors for point anomalies in metadata and simple activity features, without assuming a particular data distribution.
scenario: 要快速筛出账号元数据和基础活动特征里的孤立异常点。
options: Isolation forest
大型 sequence autoencoder
人工逐个审查全量账号
只用一个多模态 LLM
whenOtherWins: 如果异常是复杂时间序列模式，autoencoder 或序列模型更可能捕捉。
tradeoff: isolation forest 的效率 vs autoencoder 对复杂序列模式的表达力
options_en: Isolation forest.
A large sequence autoencoder.
Manually reviewing every account one by one.
Using a single multimodal LLM.
q_en: What should you try first for this anomaly screen?
scenario_en: You need to cheaply screen isolated anomalies in account metadata and basic activity features.
optionExplanations: 对高维表格特征来说，这类基于随机切分树的方法计算高效、不用假设特定的数据分布，适合拿来做元数据和基础活动特征的第一道快速筛查。
autoencoder 更适合复杂序列模式，成本远超「快速筛查」这个目标所需。
人工逐个审查在数十亿账号规模下完全不可扩展。
多模态 LLM 面向内容理解，不适合结构化的元数据特征。
optionExplanations_en: Isolation forest is efficient on high-dimensional tabular features without needing a strong distribution assumption, making it a good first-pass screen for metadata and basic activity features.
Autoencoders suit complex sequential patterns better, at a compute cost far beyond what a quick screen needs.
Manually reviewing every account one by one doesn't scale at billions of accounts.
A multimodal LLM targets content understanding, a poor fit for structured metadata features.

scenario: 要抓的异常是事件序列的节奏不像人：每个单独特征都正常，只有组合和顺序不对。
q: autoencoder 做异常检测相比 isolation forest 的优势是什么？
why: autoencoder 学习压缩重构正常行为，重构误差大代表异常；比 isolation forest 更贵，也有学会重构一切的「病理」风险。
why_en: Autoencoders can capture complex sequential and contextual patterns that isolation forests miss, at the cost of higher compute and the risk of learning to reconstruct anomalies too well.
options: 能捕捉更复杂的序列/上下文重构模式
成本永远比 isolation forest 更低
不需要定义任何重构损失
不会把异常也重构出来
tradeoff: autoencoder 的复杂模式表达力 vs isolation forest 的计算效率

termDefinitions.meaning: 学习压缩再重建正常数据，重建误差大的账号更可能异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An autoencoder learns to compress and reconstruct normal data, and a large reconstruction error flags an account as anomalous.

options_en: It can capture more complex sequential/contextual reconstruction patterns.
It is unconditionally cheaper than an isolation forest.
It needs no reconstruction loss defined at all.
It never ends up reconstructing anomalies too.
q_en: What advantage does an autoencoder have over isolation forest for anomaly detection?
scenario_en: The anomaly you need is a non-human rhythm in the event sequence: every single feature looks normal, only the combination and order are off.
optionExplanations: 压缩再重建正常行为是自编码器的强项，能捕捉基于随机切分树的筛查方法抓不住的复杂序列/上下文模式，代价是更贵。
实际成本关系是反的：跑一次自编码器通常比那种基于随机切分树的筛查方法更贵。
设计重构损失恰恰是用好 autoencoder 的关键难点。
学会把异常也重构得很好，正是 autoencoder 的已知病理风险。
optionExplanations_en: An autoencoder learns to compress and reconstruct normal behavior, catching complex sequential/contextual patterns isolation forest misses—at higher cost.
The cost relationship is actually reversed—autoencoders usually cost more than isolation forests.
