Designing the reconstruction loss is exactly the hard part of using an autoencoder well.
Learning to reconstruct anomalies too well is a known pathology risk for autoencoders.

q: 更合理的异常检测组合方式是什么？
why: 级联利用 isolation forest 的效率做第一道筛查，再用 autoencoder 深查复杂模式，融合分数按置信度组合两者结果。
why_en: A cascaded setup uses isolation forests for cheap first-pass screening and autoencoders for deeper checks on complex sequential patterns, then combines their scores.
scenario: 你既要便宜筛查，又要捕捉复杂的协调行为。
options: isolation forest 先筛，再深入复核
只用成本最贵的那一个模型直接跑全量账号
只依赖纯随机抽样的方式来筛查异常账号
彻底放弃整个异常检测这一处理环节
whenOtherWins: 如果流量很小且序列异常是唯一目标，可以直接用 autoencoder。
tradeoff: 级联组合的成本效率 vs 单一方法各自的局限
options_en: Isolation forest screens first, then a deeper recheck.
Run only that single most expensive model directly on every account.
Rely purely on a random-sampling approach alone to screen for anomalies.
Drop the entire anomaly-detection processing step altogether.
q_en: What is the better way to combine anomaly detectors?
scenario_en: You need cheap first-pass screening and still want to catch complex coordinated behavior.
optionExplanations: 用基于随机切分树的方法先便宜地筛一遍，再用更贵的自编码模型深查复杂协调模式，融合两者结果，兼顾成本和表达力。
全量账号跑最贵的模型，计算成本不可持续。
随机抽样不是针对性筛查，抓不住真正的异常。
放弃异常检测等于丢了发现新型未知 bot 模式的渠道。
optionExplanations_en: Screening cheaply with isolation forest first, then running autoencoders on the flagged subset for complex coordinated patterns, balances cost against expressive power.
Running the most expensive model on every account is an unsustainable compute cost.
Random sampling isn't targeted screening, so it misses real anomalies.
Dropping anomaly detection entirely gives up the channel for finding new, unknown bot patterns.

scenario: 异常检测每天报出 5 万个行为怪异的账号，里面有大量小众爱好者和真实运营号。
q: 为什么不能把所有「行为异常」的账号都当成 bot？
why: 异常只是调查信号，还要结合 bot 造成的实际伤害和人工验证，否则会误伤行为独特但合法的边缘真实用户。
why_en: Anomaly scores are just a signal for investigation, not proof of harm, so they must be combined with evidence of actual bot impact before any action is taken.
options: 业务关心造成 harm 的异常，而非单纯「奇怪」
异常一定百分之百都代表恶意的攻击行为
异常检测在实践中完全不会产生任何误报
行为奇怪的账号不需要任何形式的保护
options_en: The business cares about harmful anomalies, not just weirdness.
An anomaly is always, one hundred percent, a malicious attack.
Anomaly detection in practice never produces any false positive.
Accounts that behave unusually deserve no protection of any kind.
q_en: Why not treat every behaviorally unusual account as a bot?
scenario_en: Anomaly detection surfaces 50k weird-looking accounts a day, including plenty of niche hobbyists and genuine community managers.
optionExplanations: 业务真正关心的是造成伤害的异常，「行为奇怪」只是调查线索，还要结合实际伤害证据和人工验证才能定性。
很多合法用户的行为在统计上也会显得异常，不能直接等同恶意。
isolation forest 和 autoencoder 都会产生误报。
把奇怪等同该被处置，会误伤只是行为独特的合法边缘用户。
optionExplanations_en: The business really cares about anomalies that cause harm—'looking weird' is just an investigation lead that still needs harm evidence and human verification.
Plenty of legitimate behavior also looks statistically unusual, so anomaly doesn't equal malice.
Both isolation forests and autoencoders produce false positives.
Treating unusual as disposable ends up harming legitimate users who simply behave differently.

scenario: 算力有限，只有一小部分高风险账号值得跑昂贵的重模型，最后还要落到执行动作。
q: 按合理顺序排列 bot 检测系统主流程。
why: 先构造多源特征，再用轻模型省计算，重模型处理高风险集合，最后由动作层按置信度执行。
why_en: The bot pipeline gathers multi-source features, filters cheaply with a light model, scores the suspicious subset deeply, then applies calibrated actions.
steps: 根据校准风险采取封禁/降权/限流
轻量模型筛出可疑账号
收集活动、图、内容和元数据特征
重图序列模型深度评分
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Features[Activity graph content meta] --> Light[Light model]
  Light --> Heavy[Heavy score]
  Heavy --> Cal[Calibration]
  Cal --> Actions[Ban demote limit]
q_en: Put the main bot-detection system flow in the right order.
scenario_en: Compute is limited, only a small high-risk slice deserves the expensive heavy model, and everything must end in an enforcement action.

scenario: 每周只有几百条可信标签，但无标签的图和事件流海量，模型还必须输出可信概率。
q: 按正确顺序排列 bot 主模型训练策略。
why: 预训练先学平台结构，融合后再定义监督目标，最后用稀缺高质量标签微调与校准。
why_en: The training path pretrains graph and sequence encoders, aligns them, applies an impact-weighted objective, and fine-tunes with trusted labels.
steps: 用调查员标签微调并校准
图侧和序列侧自监督预训练
融合图/序列表示并做对齐
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Pre[Self-supervised pretrain] --> Fuse[Graph sequence fusion]
  Fuse --> Loss[Impact-weighted BCE]
  Loss --> Fine[Fine-tune labels]
  Fine --> Cal[Calibrate]
q_en: Put the main bot-model training strategy in the right order.
scenario_en: Only a few hundred trusted labels arrive weekly against a mountain of unlabeled graph and event data, and the model still owes calibrated probabilities.

scenario: 业务目标写成「最大化 bot 检出，误封率 <1%」。线上算力大半花在刷猫图的低危 bot 上，散播恶意链接的账号却排在后面。
scenario_en: The stated goal is "maximize bot detections with false positives under 1%". Most compute now goes to harmless cat-picture bots while malware-link accounts wait in line.
q: 「最大化检出 + 误封 <1%」这个目标漏掉了什么？
q_en: What does a "maximize detections, keep false positives under 1%" objective miss?
options: 没有按每个 bot 造成的危害加权
没有给误封设上限，用户会被误伤
把 recall 和 precision 混为一谈，无法调阈值
检出率在生产环境里根本无法测量
options_en: It does not weight bots by the harm each one causes.
It sets no cap on false positives, so real users get hit.
It confuses recall with precision, so no threshold can be tuned.
Detection rate simply cannot be measured in production.
optionExplanations: 检出数把猫图 bot 和恶意链接 bot 各记一分，资源就流向最好抓而不是最该抓的账号。
误封上限恰恰已经写在目标里了，这不是它的缺口。
recall 与 precision 定义不同但都可算，阈值照样能调。
检出数、误封率都能用抽样标注在线上估计出来。
optionExplanations_en: Counting detections scores a cat-picture bot and a malware bot alike, so effort flows to the easiest catches rather than the most harmful ones.
The false-positive cap is already written into this objective, so that is not the gap.
Recall and precision are defined differently but both computable; thresholds remain tunable.
Both detection counts and false-positive rates can be estimated online via sampled labeling.
why: 按检出个数计分等于假设所有 bot 危害相同，资源会向易抓的低危账号倾斜。改成影响加权的代价是要额外设计伤害度量。
why_en: Counting detections treats every bot as equally harmful, so resources drift toward easy low-harm accounts; moving to an impact-weighted objective costs you a harm metric you now have to design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把真实用户误判成 bot 的情况。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is a legitimate user wrongly classified as a bot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有真实 bot 中被模型抓到的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of all real bots that the model actually catches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型判为 bot 的账号中真的是 bot 的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of flagged accounts that really are bots.

scenario: 真实用户被判 bot 后账号被限流，唯一出路是申诉；调查员每周只能查数百个账号，而 bot 作者同样熟练地批量提交申诉。
scenario_en: A real user flagged as a bot gets restricted and can only appeal; investigators handle just a few hundred accounts a week, and bot authors file appeals just as fluently.
q: 误封一个真实用户的代价链是怎么走完的？
q_en: How does the full cost chain of one wrongful ban play out?
options: 限流→申诉→占用稀缺人工，bot 也会刷申诉
只损失该用户当天一次会话，之后会自动恢复
申诉全部由模型自动裁决，不消耗人工预算
误封只影响离线指标，不改变真实用户行为
options_en: Restriction, then appeal, then scarce human review that bots also flood.
The user loses one session that day and recovers automatically after.
Appeals are all decided by a model, consuming no human budget.
Wrongful bans only move offline metrics, not real user behavior.
optionExplanations: 被限流的用户只能排进人工申诉队列，而这条队列同时被 bot 作者占用。
限制不会自己解除，用户得主动申诉才可能恢复访问。
判定是否误封需要人工调查，这正是稀缺资源所在。
被误封的用户会流失参与度甚至离开平台，影响是真实的。
optionExplanations_en: A restricted user can only join the human appeals queue, which bot authors are crowding at the same time.
Restrictions do not lift themselves; the user must appeal to regain access.
Deciding whether a ban was wrong needs human investigation, which is exactly the scarce resource.
Wrongly banned users lose engagement and may leave the platform, so the impact is real.
why: 误封把用户推进申诉队列，而队列消耗的正是每周只有数百个名额的调查员预算，bot 作者还会一起刷。代价：误伤越多，能查真 bot 的人工越少。
why_en: A wrongful ban pushes the user into an appeals queue that burns the same few-hundred-per-week investigator budget bots also exploit, so every false positive steals review capacity from real bot hunting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被处置的账号请求人工复核处置结果的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An appeal is the process where a restricted account asks a human to review the enforcement decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由调查员人工确认的、可信度最高的账号标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ground truth label is the high-trust verdict an investigator produces by hand.

scenario: bot 若不治理会占平台一半以上动作。有人据此主张：既然治理省下的算力多于治理花掉的算力，检测链路就不必再优化。
scenario_en: Left alone, bots would drive over half of all platform actions. Someone argues that since remediation saves more compute than it burns, the detection path needs no further optimization.
q: 「bot 治理净 compute 为正」该怎么正确使用？
q_en: How should the "bot remediation is compute-positive" argument actually be used?
options: 它说明治理值得做，但不豁免效率要求
它说明检测链路可以随意堆重模型
它说明检测应该只放在离线批处理里做
它说明可以对每条内容都跑一次大模型
options_en: It shows remediation is worth doing, but does not excuse inefficiency.
It means the detection path can freely stack heavy models.
It means detection belongs only in offline batch jobs.
It means you can run a large model over every single piece of content.
optionExplanations: 净收益为正只回答「要不要做」，预算问题还得单独算。
检测跑在注册、发帖等高频交互面前，堆重模型会直接推高延迟与成本。
离线批处理抓不住新注册账号的即时风险，实时触发是必须的。
逐条内容跑大模型的开销远超收益，也谈不上净正。
optionExplanations_en: Being net-positive answers whether to do it at all; the budget question still has to be sized separately.
Detection sits in front of registration and posting, so stacking heavy models directly raises latency and cost.
Offline batches miss the immediate risk from freshly registered accounts, so real-time triggering is required.
Running a large model per item costs far more than it returns, and would not stay net-positive.
why: 净收益为正是「值不值得做」的答案，不是「能花多少」的答案；检测挡在大量用户交互面前，算力仍是硬约束。代价：得靠级联和缓存把成本压下来。
why_en: Compute-positive answers whether remediation is worth doing, not how much it may spend; detection sits in front of huge interaction volume, so you still pay for cascading and caching to keep it affordable.
tradeoff: 治理的净算力收益为正 vs 检测链路自身的算力预算
whenOtherWins: 如果某类攻击伤害极高且只是短期爆发，可以临时接受更贵的检测链路先止血，事后再优化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量模型过滤，只把可疑账号交给重模型，节省大部分算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading inference filters with a cheap model first and sends only suspicious accounts to the heavy model.

scenario: 平台已有一支低质内容治理团队。bot 团队想把「减少 spam 曝光」当作自己的主指标，但两套系统会对同一批内容采取动作。
scenario_en: The platform already has a low-quality-content team. The bot team wants "reduced spam impressions" as its headline metric, but both systems act on the same content.
q: bot 治理与低质内容治理的职责边界怎么划？
q_en: How should responsibility split between bot remediation and low-quality-content systems?
options: 并非所有低质内容来自 bot，指标要能归因
两套系统合并成一套，用同一个模型判
bot 系统放弃影响类指标，只看封禁数量
低质内容系统停用，全部交给 bot 系统处理
options_en: Not all low-quality content comes from bots, so the metric must be attributable.
Merge the two systems and judge everything with one model.
The bot system drops impact metrics and tracks ban counts only.
Retire the low-quality-content system and hand everything to bot detection.
optionExplanations: 真人也会发垃圾内容，spam 曝光下降未必是 bot 系统的功劳。
两者的信号源和处置手段不同，强行合并会让账号级证据被内容级判断淹没。
封禁数量会重新激励过度封禁，回到被否掉的目标上。
停掉内容侧治理会放过全部由真人产出的低质内容。
optionExplanations_en: Real humans post junk too, so a drop in spam impressions is not automatically the bot system's win.
The two use different signals and enforcement levers; merging drowns account-level evidence in content-level judgement.
Ban counts re-create the over-enforcement incentive that was already rejected.
Shutting down content moderation lets through all the low-quality content produced by real people.
why: 影响类指标最贴近用户体验，但 spam 曝光同时被两套系统改动，不做归因就分不清是谁的效果。代价：要额外设计能归因到账号来源的指标口径。
why_en: Impact metrics track user experience best, but two systems move spam impressions at once, so without attribution you cannot tell whose change worked — and building attributable metric definitions costs extra design.
tradeoff: 指标贴近用户体验 vs 指标能归因到本系统
whenOtherWins: 如果平台上低质内容几乎全部由 botnet 产出，两套系统合并确实能省掉重复建设。

termDefinitions.meaning: 垃圾内容被真实用户看到的次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spam impression is one view of junk content by a real user.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由同一作者协同操控的一大批 bot 账号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A botnet is a large set of bot accounts operated together by one author.

scenario: 非参数分支把已知 bot 的内容和账号放进 ANN 索引，命中近邻就判风险；为了跟上新模式，系统把自己判出的 bot 也自动写回索引。
scenario_en: The non-parametric branch indexes known bot content and accounts in an ANN store and flags whatever lands near them; to keep up with new patterns it writes its own verdicts back into the index.
q: 把系统自判结果自动写回近邻索引，会怎么一步步失效？
q_en: How does auto-writing the system's own verdicts back into the neighbor index fail, step by step?
options: 误判进索引→更多相似账号被判中→索引越滚越偏
索引体积不变，只是近邻查询延迟缓慢升高
索引会拒绝新写入，导致新 bot 模式全部漏检
近邻距离保持恒定，模型分数只会整体下降
options_en: A false positive enters the index, pulls in more similar accounts, and the index drifts further each round.
Index size stays flat and only neighbor-query latency creeps upward.
The index refuses new writes, so every new bot pattern goes undetected.
Neighbor distances stay constant and scores merely shift downward overall.
optionExplanations: 一个误判的良性账号成为「已知 bot」样本后，会把和它相似的良性账号一起拖下水。
索引会持续变大，问题也不在延迟而在内容被污染。
写回路径是开着的，失效恰恰来自写进去的东西不可信。
索引内容变了，近邻距离必然跟着变，分数也不是单向下降。
optionExplanations_en: Once a wrongly flagged benign account becomes a "known bot" exemplar, it drags accounts similar to it down with it.
The index keeps growing, and the problem is contaminated content rather than latency.
The write path is open; the failure comes precisely from writing untrustworthy entries into it.
Index contents change, so neighbor distances change too, and scores do not simply drift one way.
why: 索引里存的是「什么算 bot」的定义，写回自判结果就让误判自我复制，良性数据被越索引越多，形成 runaway 反馈循环。修法：ground truth 标签与系统标签分开存并按可信度加权。
why_en: The index defines what counts as a bot, so feeding it the system's own verdicts lets false positives replicate and pull benign data in — which is why investigator labels must be stored and weighted separately from system-generated ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：在向量库里快速找出与查询最像的若干条。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN, Approximate Nearest Neighbor search, quickly finds the entries in a vector store most similar to a query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不训练固定参数，直接用检索到的相似样本来判断的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A non-parametric method makes decisions by retrieving similar stored examples instead of learning fixed parameters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统输出被当成输入回喂，偏差被一轮轮放大的循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A runaway feedback loop is when a system's own output is fed back as input, amplifying its bias each round.

scenario: 当前这批 bot 靠固定文案模板露馅，换个模板就抓不到；下一代 bot 已经在用 LLM 现生成内容。
scenario_en: Today's bots give themselves away with fixed copy templates and vanish the moment they rotate templates; the next generation already generates posts with an LLM.
q: 特征集怎么组合才不会 bot 一改招就失灵？
q_en: How should the feature set be composed so it does not die the moment bots change tactics?
options: 易得信号抓当下，行为节奏类信号抗漂移
只保留当前命中率最高的那批模板特征
全部换成最抽象的特征，放弃易得信号
每次 bot 变招就把模型整体重训一遍
options_en: Keep easy wins for today's bots plus rhythm-based signals that survive adaptation.
Keep only the template features with the best current hit rate.
Replace everything with the most abstract features and drop the easy wins.
Retrain the whole model from scratch every time bots change tactics.
optionExplanations: 两类特征分别覆盖「现在能抓到」和「明年还管用」，缺一边都会塌。
模板特征命中率高但寿命短，攻击者一改文案就整批失效。
放弃易得信号会牺牲眼下的召回，低级 bot 会立刻回流。
重训解决不了特征本身已经不含信息的问题。
optionExplanations_en: The two kinds cover "catches bots today" and "still works next year"; drop either side and coverage collapses.
Template features hit hard but die young — one copy rewrite retires the whole batch.
Dropping easy wins sacrifices near-term recall and low-effort bots flood straight back.
Retraining cannot fix features that no longer carry any signal at all.
why: 易得特征命中快但攻击者一改就废，作息与反应时间这类节奏信号难伪造却更弱，所以两类要同时留在特征集里。代价：维护两套特征的成本和复杂度都翻倍。
why_en: Easy features hit fast but die when attackers adapt, while rhythm signals like sleep cycles are hard to fake yet individually weaker, so you carry both — and pay double the feature-maintenance cost.
tradeoff: 抓当下 bot 的易得信号 vs 抗对抗漂移的根本信号
whenOtherWins: 如果面对的是一次性、短周期的攻击活动，先上易得的模板特征止血，比追求长期稳健更划算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者持续调整手法，导致模型学到的分布随时间失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adversarial drift is attackers continuously changing tactics so the distribution a model learned stops holding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，可用来批量生成看起来自然的帖子内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LLM, or Large Language Model, can mass-produce posts that read as naturally written.

scenario: 序列模型要读约 200 个事件才出分，但平台有 5 亿日活、每人 1-2 次会话，不可能对每个动作都跑一遍。
scenario_en: The sequence model reads roughly 200 events before scoring, but with 500M daily active users at one to two sessions each, it cannot run on every single action.
q: 活动节奏信号在实时链路上该怎么落地？
q_en: How should activity-rhythm signals be delivered on the real-time path?
options: 用多时间窗的手工统计特征做折中
对每个动作都实时跑一遍序列模型
干脆放弃活动节奏这一整类信号
把序列模型换成更大的 transformer
options_en: Compromise with hand-engineered statistics over multiple time windows.
Run the full sequence model on every action in real time.
Drop the entire activity-rhythm signal family.
Swap the sequence model for a larger transformer.
optionExplanations: 间隔分布、方差、熵按小时/天/周各算一份，成本是几个聚合而不是一次前向。
算力预算撑不住，检测又挡在高频交互面前，延迟会直接外溢给用户。
节奏类信号恰恰是最难伪造的一类，放弃等于把最稳的证据丢掉。
换更大的模型让每次推理更贵，与「跑不起」这个约束正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Inter-event gaps, variance and entropy computed hourly, daily and weekly cost a few aggregations instead of a forward pass.
The compute budget cannot absorb it, and since detection gates high-frequency interactions the latency lands on users.
Rhythm signals are the hardest to fake, so dropping them throws away the most durable evidence.
A bigger model makes each inference more expensive, which is the opposite of the binding constraint.
why: 理想情况这些节奏由序列模型自己学，但它跑不到每个动作上；多窗口的统计量是可负担的替代。代价：手工特征会漏掉模型才能学到的组合模式。
why_en: Ideally the sequence model learns these rhythms itself, but it cannot run per action, so multi-window statistics are the affordable stand-in — at the cost of missing combinations only a learned model would find.
tradeoff: 序列模型学到的时序细节 vs 手工统计特征的算力成本
whenOtherWins: 账号已被轻量模型判为可疑、进入级联的重模型阶段时，跑完整序列模型是值得的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一组行为分布有多不规则，太低说明动作过于规律。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entropy measures how irregular a behavior distribution is; very low entropy means suspiciously regular actions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于自注意力的序列模型，表达力强但推理成本高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transformer is a self-attention sequence model with high expressiveness and high inference cost.

scenario: 一批 bot 共用少量代理 IP 和同一台服务器，登录节奏也和真人不同。你要从账号元数据里挑出认证模式这一组特征。
scenario_en: A bot batch shares a handful of proxy IPs and one machine, and its login rhythm does not look human. You are picking the authentication-pattern group out of account metadata.
q: 账号元数据里的认证模式特征包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which account-metadata features belong to the authentication-pattern group? (Select all that apply.)
options: 登录频率
设备多样性
地理位置一致性
帖子的语义多样性
options_en: Login frequency.
Device diversity.
Location consistency.
Semantic diversity across posts.
optionExplanations: 登录频率：脚本化的登录节奏过于规律或过密，暴露非人操作。
设备多样性：一台机器批量控号时，设备指纹会异常集中。
地理位置一致性：同一账号短时间跨地登录，说明它被程序共用。
语义多样性属于内容信号那一组，不由认证行为产生。
optionExplanations_en: Login frequency: scripted logins are too regular or too dense, exposing non-human operation.
Device diversity: when one machine drives many accounts, device fingerprints cluster abnormally.
Location consistency: the same account logging in from far apart within minutes means a program is sharing it.
Semantic diversity belongs to the content-signal group and is not produced by authentication behavior.
why: 认证类特征刻画的是「谁在什么机器上、从哪里登进来」，对低成本批量控号的 bot 特别有效。代价：高级攻击者用住宅代理和指纹伪装就能削弱它们。
why_en: Authentication features describe who logs in from which machine and where, which catches cheap mass-controlled bots — though residential proxies and fingerprint spoofing weaken them against sophisticated attackers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由浏览器、系统、硬件属性拼出的设备标识。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A device fingerprint is an identifier assembled from browser, OS and hardware attributes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中转服务器的地址，用来隐藏账号真实来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy IP is a relay server address used to hide where an account really connects from.

scenario: 检测系统已经在线跑了一段时间，每个账号都积累了一份与检测系统交互的历史，这份历史本身可以回喂模型。
scenario_en: The detection system has been live for a while, so every account has a history of interacting with it, and that history can itself be fed back as features.
q: 哪些实时行为信号可以当特征回喂 bot 模型？（多选）
q_en: Which real-time behavioral signals can be fed back as features to the bot model? (Select all that apply.)
options: 被各模型标记的历史次数
被标记之后行为的变化
申诉的频率与成功率
注册时填写的生日
options_en: How often the account has been flagged across models.
How behavior changes after being flagged.
Appeal frequency and success rate.
The birthday entered at registration.
optionExplanations: 跨模型的累计标记次数：把多个模型各自的弱信号叠成一条强证据。
标记后的行为突变：说明账号在主动适应检测规则。
申诉频率与成功率：高频提交但极少成功，本身就是可疑模式。
生日是注册时的静态资料字段，不是与检测系统交互产生的信号。
optionExplanations_en: Cumulative cross-model flag counts stack several weak per-model signals into one strong piece of evidence.
A behavior jump right after a flag shows the account is actively adapting to the rules.
Filing appeals constantly while almost never winning is itself a suspicious pattern.
Birthday is a static registration field, not a signal generated by interacting with detection.
why: 这些信号只有在系统上线运行后才存在，价值在于它们记录的是账号对检测本身的反应。代价：新注册账号完全没有这类特征，模型必须容忍缺失值。
why_en: These signals only exist once the system has been running, and their value is that they record how an account reacts to detection itself — the cost being that brand-new accounts have none, so the model must tolerate missing values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 账号申诉被判定为误封的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Appeal success rate is the share of an account's appeals that are ruled wrongful enforcement.

scenario: 一个账号被限流后 24 小时内，把整点固定的发帖间隔改成随机抖动，还换掉了设备指纹；真实用户被限流时不会这样反应。
scenario_en: Within a day of being restricted, an account switches from posting on the hour to randomized jitter and swaps its device fingerprint — not how a real restricted user reacts.
q: 这种「被标记后行为突变」最好怎么用？
q_en: What is the best use of a behavior jump right after an account gets flagged?
options: 当成规避信号，作为特征喂回模型
当成账号已改邪归正，调低风险分
忽略它，只看被标记之前的行为
直接据此永久封禁，不再经过模型
options_en: Treat it as an evasion signal and feed it back to the model as a feature.
Read it as the account reforming and lower its risk score.
Ignore it and score only on pre-flag behavior.
Permanently ban on this alone, bypassing the model.
optionExplanations: 规避动作本身携带信息：只有知道自己被检测的一方才会这样调整。
风险分调低正中攻击者下怀，改一次参数就能洗白。
只看标记前行为等于自愿丢掉一整类对抗性证据。
单一信号直接触发永久处置，会绕过校准好的误封上限。
optionExplanations_en: The evasion move carries information: only someone who knows they were detected adjusts this way.
Lowering the score is exactly what the attacker wants — one parameter change and the account is clean.
Scoring only pre-flag behavior voluntarily discards an entire class of adversarial evidence.
Letting one signal trigger permanent enforcement bypasses the calibrated false-positive guardrail.
why: bot 的规避尝试反而证明它在适应检测，于是攻击者每躲一次就留下一条新证据，形成对抗反馈循环。代价：真实用户的正常行为变化会被误读，需要其他信号交叉验证。
why_en: A bot's evasion attempt proves it is adapting to detection, so every dodge leaves a fresh signal behind — the cost is that ordinary behavior changes by real users can be misread, so it needs corroborating signals.
tradeoff: 把规避动作读成证据 vs 读成账号行为改善
whenOtherWins: 如果限流本身来自模型误判，真实用户随之减少发帖就不该算规避，要结合申诉结果一起判断。

termDefinitions.meaning: 账号在察觉被检测后为躲避处置而做出的行为改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An evasion pattern is how an account changes behavior once it senses it has been detected.

termDefinitions.meaning: 攻击者的躲避动作被系统采集成新的检测信号的循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An adversarial feedback loop is when the attacker's dodging itself becomes a new detection signal.

scenario: 面试官问你是否一开始就把图模型、序列模型、异常检测全部端上来。线上攻击手法每个季度都在变，你也说不准下一个缺口在哪。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether you would ship the graph model, sequence model and anomaly detection all at once. Attack tactics rotate every quarter and the next gap is unknown.
q: bot 检测的多层防御该怎么建立起来？
q_en: How should the layered defense of a bot-detection system be built up?
options: 先上简单一层，按真实攻击暴露的缺口加层
一次性把全部层级都设计完，再统一上线交付
只保留最强的那一层，其余全部删掉
每发现一种新攻击就把整套系统重写
options_en: Start with one simple layer and add layers where real attacks expose gaps.
Design every single layer up front, then launch them all together.
Keep only the single strongest layer and delete the rest.
Rewrite the whole system each time a new attack appears.
optionExplanations: 安全系统是被真实攻击喂出来的，先简单再补，才补在真的缺口上。
提前设计的层往往挡的是想象中的攻击，上线后仍要重做。
只留一层就没有安全网，这层被绕过时整套防线一起失守。
重写成本极高，而攻击手法的变化频率远高于系统能重写的频率。
optionExplanations_en: Security systems are grown by real attacks; starting simple and patching afterwards puts layers where the gaps truly are.
Layers designed up front tend to block imagined attacks and still get reworked after launch.
A single layer leaves no safety net, so the whole defense falls the moment it is bypassed.
Rewrites are expensive, and tactics change far faster than a system can be rewritten.
why: 攻击手法一直在变，提前设计的层挡不到真实缺口；多层的价值在于互为安全网，任何一层被绕过还有下一层接着。代价：层数越多，运维负担与推理延迟越高。
why_en: Tactics keep shifting so pre-designed layers rarely sit where the real gaps are; layers earn their keep as each other's safety net, at the price of more operational burden and inference latency.
tradeoff: 一次把防御设计到位 vs 按真实攻击有机分层生长
whenOtherWins: 如果面对的是已知成熟攻击面（比如批量注册），直接照搬业界成型的多层方案比从零试错更快。

termDefinitions.term: defense in depth / 纵深防御
termDefinitions.meaning: 安全原则：叠多层独立防线，任一层被突破仍有后续层兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Defense in depth is the security principle of stacking independent layers so a breach of one still meets another.

scenario: 图分支用 GraphSAGE 聚合 2 跳邻域。有人主张简化实现：把 follow 边和 reply 边当成同一种边一起聚合。
scenario_en: The graph branch aggregates a two-hop neighborhood with GraphSAGE. Someone proposes simplifying it by aggregating follow edges and reply edges as a single edge type.
q: 把 follow 边和 reply 边一视同仁会怎么坏事？
q_en: What breaks if follow edges and reply edges are aggregated as the same relation?
options: 自动关注上千人的账号会长得像社区核心
邻居采样会失效，fan-out 无法再封顶
模型会退化成 transductive，无法嵌入新节点
2 跳邻域会自动扩张成一次全图遍历
options_en: An account that auto-follows thousands starts to look like a well-connected community hub.
Neighbor sampling breaks and fan-out can no longer be capped.
The model degrades to transductive and cannot embed new nodes.
The two-hop neighborhood silently expands into a full graph traversal.
optionExplanations: follow 边可以单方面批量制造，堆够数量就把 spammer 的连接度顶上去了。
邻居采样按数量截断，和边类型区不区分无关。
GraphSAGE 的归纳性来自邻域聚合函数，不由边权决定。
跳数上限仍是 2，边类型合并不会改变遍历深度。
optionExplanations_en: Follow edges can be manufactured unilaterally in bulk, so enough of them push a spammer's connectivity right up.
Neighbor sampling truncates by count and is unaffected by whether edge types are distinguished.
GraphSAGE's inductive property comes from its aggregation function, not from edge weights.
The hop limit is still two; merging edge types does not change traversal depth.
why: follow 是单方面动作，reply 需要对方参与，可信度天然不同；一视同仁聚合时上千条自动关注就被读成社区核心的特征。relation-specific weights 让两类边分开加权。
why_en: A follow is unilateral while a reply needs the other side to engage, so relation-specific weights let GraphSAGE discount auto-follows instead of reading thousands of them as community centrality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归纳式图神经网络，靠采样邻居并聚合来生成节点表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphSAGE is an inductive graph neural network that embeds a node by sampling and aggregating its neighbors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按边的类型使用不同的聚合权重，让不同关系贡献不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relation-specific weights give each edge type its own aggregation weight so different relations contribute differently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只能处理训练时见过的节点、新节点需重训的图模型性质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transductive means the model only handles nodes seen during training and needs retraining for new ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个节点连接的邻居数量，名人账号扇出极大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is how many neighbors a node has, and celebrity accounts have enormous fan-out.

scenario: 图编码器和序列编码器各自自监督预训练完毕，中间的 cross-attention 融合层还没训练，而调查员标签一条都还没舍得用。
scenario_en: The graph and sequence encoders finished self-supervised pretraining, the cross-attention fusion layer is untrained, and not a single investigator label has been spent yet.
q: 融合层的无标签对齐预训练目标是什么？
q_en: What is the objective of the label-free alignment pass over the fusion layer?
options: 同账号的两路表示靠近，不同账号推开
让两路表示完全相同，抹掉分支差异
直接用二分类交叉熵，标签取系统判定结果
冻结融合层，等到微调阶段再训练它
options_en: Pull the two views of one account together and push different accounts apart.
Force the two views to be identical, erasing branch differences.
Train binary cross-entropy directly, using system verdicts as labels.
Freeze the fusion layer and train it only during fine-tuning.
optionExplanations: 奖励一致、惩罚混淆，融合层就学会「这两路说的是同一个账号」。
两路完全相同就没有互补信息了，cross-attention 也失去意义。
拿系统判定当标签会把模型自身的偏差固化进融合层。
不训练融合层，稀缺的调查员标签就得同时承担对齐和判别两件事。
optionExplanations_en: Rewarding agreement and punishing confusion teaches the layer that both views describe one account.
If both views became identical there would be no complementary information left for cross-attention to use.
Using system verdicts as labels bakes the model's own bias into the fusion layer.
Skipping this pass makes the scarce investigator labels do alignment and discrimination at the same time.
why: 对齐先让融合层学会「同一个账号的图视角与时序视角是同一件事」，完全不消耗标签。代价：它只学到一致性，判别 bot 仍要靠后续的有标签微调和校准。
why_en: The alignment pass teaches the fusion layer that an account's graph view and timeline view describe the same entity without spending a label, but it only learns consistency — telling bots apart still needs supervised fine-tuning and calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一路表示去查询另一路表示的注意力机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-attention lets one representation query another so the two branches can inform each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把账号或事件压成的稠密向量表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector that represents an account or an event.

scenario: 账号收到用户举报需要重新评估。图 embedding 要拉 2 跳邻域重算，代价很高，但这个账号这周的关注关系几乎没有变动。
scenario_en: A user report triggers re-evaluation. Recomputing the graph embedding means pulling a two-hop neighborhood, which is expensive, yet this account's connections barely moved this week.
q: 重新触发评估时怎么压住重算成本？
q_en: How do you keep the cost of a re-triggered evaluation down?
options: 复用缓存的图 embedding，只刷新行为特征
两侧特征全部重算一遍，保证绝对新鲜
跳过这次评估，等每日批处理统一算
只重算图 embedding，行为特征沿用缓存
options_en: Reuse the cached graph embedding and refresh only the behavioral features.
Recompute both sides in full to guarantee absolute freshness.
Skip this evaluation and let the daily batch job handle it.
Recompute only the graph embedding and reuse cached behavioral features.
optionExplanations: 贵的那一半没变就不必重算，便宜的那一半才需要跟上最新动作。
全量重算把最贵的一步做成了每次触发的固定开销。
举报正是需要快速响应的信号，压到次日会放任伤害继续累积。
正好搞反了：变化快的是行为特征，图邻域反而相对稳定。
optionExplanations_en: The expensive half has not changed, so only the cheap half needs to catch up with recent actions.
Full recomputation turns the most expensive step into a fixed cost on every trigger.
A report is exactly the signal that needs a fast response; deferring it lets harm keep accumulating.
This inverts the picture: behavioral features move fast while the graph neighborhood is comparatively stable.
why: 行为特征几小时就变，图 embedding 只在邻域变动时才会变，所以邻域没明显变化时复用缓存能让重触发变得廉价。代价：邻域悄悄变化时用到的是过期的图表示。
why_en: Behavioral features shift within hours while a graph embedding only moves when the neighborhood does, so reusing the cache makes re-triggering cheap — at the risk of scoring on a stale graph view when the neighborhood quietly changed.
tradeoff: 重算带来的新鲜度 vs 图 embedding 的计算成本
whenOtherWins: 如果账号刚刚批量关注了一大批新账号，邻域已经变了，就必须重算图 embedding。

termDefinitions.meaning: 从目标节点出发最多走 k 步能到达的所有节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-hop neighborhood is every node reachable within k steps from the target node.

scenario: 图分支上线三个月，团队想知道「靠图连接」到底比单账号特征多抓到了什么，但 PR-AUC 只给出一个混在一起的总分。
scenario_en: Three months after the graph branch shipped, the team wants to know what graph connectivity actually added over per-account features, but PR-AUC returns one blended number.
q: 哪个离线诊断指标能回答这个问题？
q_en: Which offline diagnostic metric answers that question?
options: Network Coverage：靠图连接检出的 bot 簇比例
Early Detection Rate：24 小时内检出的比例
Precision@Recall90：操作点上的精确率
PR-AUC：precision-recall 曲线下的面积
options_en: Network Coverage: the share of bot clusters caught through graph connections.
Early Detection Rate: the share of bots caught within 24 hours.
Precision@Recall90: precision at the enforcement operating point.
PR-AUC: the area under the precision-recall curve.
optionExplanations: 它直接以「簇」为单位统计，正好对应协同 botnet 这个图分支要解决的问题。
它衡量的是抓得多早，与信号来自哪一路无关。
它对齐自动处置的阈值，回答的是能不能上线的问题。
它反映整体判别力，恰恰把各路信号的贡献混在了一起。
optionExplanations_en: It counts in clusters, which maps exactly onto the coordinated-botnet problem the graph branch exists to solve.
It measures how early bots are caught, regardless of which signal found them.
It aligns with the enforcement threshold and answers whether a model is shippable.
It reports overall discriminative power, which is precisely what blends the signal contributions together.
why: 总体指标把所有信号混成一个分数，答不出「图这一路值不值」；Network Coverage 直接度量有多少 bot 簇是通过图连接抓到的。代价：它只是诊断指标，不能单独决定上不上线。
why_en: Aggregate metrics blend every signal into one score and cannot say whether the graph branch earns its cost, while Network Coverage counts bot clusters found through graph links — but it is diagnostic only and cannot decide a launch alone.
tradeoff: 总体判别力指标 vs 定位单一信号贡献的诊断指标
whenOtherWins: 如果要判断模型整体是否变好、能不能上线，PR-AUC 这类总体指标才是该看的。

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线诊断指标：有多少比例的 bot 簇是靠图连接被检出的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Network Coverage is a diagnostic metric for the percentage of bot clusters detected through graph connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: precision-recall 曲线下的面积，类别不平衡时比 ROC-AUC 更可靠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PR-AUC, the area under the precision-recall curve, is more reliable than ROC-AUC under class imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: bot 在开始活动后 24 小时内被检出的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Early Detection Rate is the fraction of bots caught within their first 24 hours of activity.

scenario: 模型把「设备多样性低 + 地理位置跳变」当作强信号，而某些地区的用户大量共用网吧设备和运营商代理，整体误封率仍稳在 1% 以下。
scenario_en: The model leans on low device diversity plus location jumps, yet in some regions users share internet-cafe machines and carrier proxies — while the overall false-positive rate still reads under 1%.
q: 评估里必须加哪一项才能发现这个问题？
q_en: What must the evaluation add in order to surface this problem?
options: 按人群和地域分层，逐层看误封率
只确认整体误封率低于 1% 的红线
加大红队模拟规避样本在测试集中的占比
把验证集改成按时间先后分层切分
options_en: Break false-positive rate down by demographic and geography.
Just confirm the overall false-positive rate stays under the 1% line.
Raise the share of red-team evasion samples in the test set.
Re-split the validation set chronologically by time.
optionExplanations: 把误封率拆到人群和地域上，才看得见某个社群单独承担了全部配额。
总体数字达标恰恰是问题所在，它把局部集中的伤害平均掉了。
红队测的是模型挡不挡得住新攻击，不回答谁被误伤。
时间分层针对的是对抗漂移，与人群间的分布差异无关。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting the false-positive rate by community and region is what reveals that one group absorbs the entire quota.
The aggregate number passing is exactly the problem — it averages away harm that is concentrated locally.
Red-teaming tests whether the model withstands new attacks, not who gets wrongly hit.
Time-based splits target adversarial drift, not differences in distribution across populations.
why: 1% 的整体误封上限完全可以由某一个社群独自承担，聚合数字看不出来；按人群和地域分层评估才能暴露不成比例的误伤。代价：分层后每层样本变少，结论噪声更大。
why_en: A single community can absorb the entire 1% false-positive budget without the aggregate number moving, so you evaluate per demographic and geography — accepting that each slice has fewer samples and noisier conclusions.
tradeoff: 整体误封率达标 vs 各人群误封率均衡
whenOtherWins: 如果关心的是模型对未来新型 bot 的稳健性，按时间分层的验证集才是对的工具。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按人群、地域等切片检查模型表现是否存在系统性偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fairness evaluation checks model performance across demographic and geographic slices for systematic bias.

scenario: 模型在历史 bot 样本上表现很好，但攻击者每季度换一次手法，等新样本进测试集时那波攻击早已跑完。
scenario_en: The model scores well on historical bot samples, but attackers rotate tactics quarterly and by the time new samples reach the test set that wave is long over.
q: 怎么在新攻击到来之前评估模型的对抗鲁棒性？
q_en: How do you evaluate adversarial robustness before the next attack arrives?
options: 维护 red team 数据集，定期用模拟规避手法测
把历史 bot 测试集扩大十倍，覆盖更多已知样本
统一把封禁阈值调低，宁可多误伤也不漏检
等真实攻击发生后，再把新样本补进测试集
options_en: Maintain a red-team dataset and regularly test against simulated evasion techniques.
Grow the historical bot test set tenfold to cover more known samples.
Lower the ban threshold across the board, accepting more false positives.
Wait for a real attack, then add the new samples to the test set.
optionExplanations: 主动构造还没出现过的规避手法，把评估的时间轴推到攻击之前。
样本再多也全是已见过的手法，覆盖不到下一代攻击。
调阈值是处置策略，不产生任何关于鲁棒性的信息，还会撞破误封红线。
这正是当前的做法，评估永远滞后于攻击一个周期。
optionExplanations_en: Constructing evasion techniques that have not appeared yet moves evaluation ahead of the attack.
More samples of already-seen tactics still cover none of the next generation of attacks.
Threshold tuning is an enforcement policy; it yields no robustness information and breaks the false-positive guardrail.
That is the current behavior, which keeps evaluation one full cycle behind the attackers.
why: 历史测试集只能证明模型挡得住见过的攻击；红队数据集主动构造规避手法，能在攻击真正到来前暴露弱点。代价：红队样本是人造的，可能猜错攻击者的下一步。
why_en: A historical test set only proves the model stops attacks it has already seen, whereas a red-team dataset manufactures evasion techniques to expose weaknesses early — at the risk that your simulated tactics guess the attacker's next move wrong.
tradeoff: 真实攻击后补样本 vs 主动模拟规避手法预演
whenOtherWins: 如果攻击面稳定、几乎没有对手在适应（比如封闭的内部系统），扩充历史测试集就够用了。

termDefinitions.meaning: 扮演攻击者、主动构造攻击样本来检验防御的团队或数据集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A red team plays the attacker, building attack samples on purpose to test whether the defense holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型在攻击者主动规避下仍保持有效的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adversarial robustness is a model staying effective while attackers actively try to evade it.

scenario: 无监督分支用 isolation forest 找未知 bot。现在有一个 5 万账号的 botnet，它们行为高度一致，而且这套行为本身就很反常。
scenario_en: The unsupervised branch uses an isolation forest to find unknown bots. A 50,000-account botnet now behaves in near-lockstep, and that shared behavior is itself unusual.
q: isolation forest 在这个 botnet 上会怎么失手？
q_en: How does an isolation forest fail on this botnet?
options: 5 万相似账号不再「少而不同」，路径变长
随机树的深度会溢出，训练过程直接失败
它无法处理缺失值，这批账号会被整批丢弃
它必须先见过 bot 标签，才能给出异常分
options_en: Fifty thousand lookalikes stop being "few and different", so their paths get longer.
Random tree depth overflows and training fails outright.
It cannot handle missing values, so the whole batch is dropped.
It needs to have seen bot labels before it can produce an anomaly score.
optionExplanations: 这批账号在特征空间里形成一个稠密簇，随机划分要切很多刀才能分开。
树深度有上限也可控，训练不会因样本相似而崩掉。
随机划分天然能容忍缺失值，这正是它的优点之一。
isolation forest 是无监督方法，本来就不需要标签。
optionExplanations_en: The batch forms a dense cluster in feature space, so random splits need many cuts to separate them.
Tree depth is bounded and controlled; training does not crash because samples look alike.
Random splitting tolerates missing values naturally — that is one of its selling points.
An isolation forest is unsupervised and needs no labels at all.
why: 它假设异常「少而不同」，几刀就能隔离；协同 botnet 形成稠密簇后平均路径长度接近正常账号，异常分掉下来，整群漏检。补位方案是能捕捉时序共性的 autoencoder。
why_en: It assumes anomalies are few and different so a few splits isolate them, but a coordinated botnet forms a dense cluster whose average path length looks normal, dropping the score and missing the whole group — which is why an autoencoder covers that case.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无监督异常检测：随机划分特征空间，越少刀就被切出来的点越异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation forest detects anomalies unsupervised: points that random splits isolate in fewer cuts are more anomalous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个样本在随机树中被单独隔离所需的划分次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Path length is how many random splits it takes to isolate one sample in a tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一行为在某些时间或网络环境下正常、换个环境才可疑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A contextual anomaly is behavior that is normal in one timing or network context and suspicious in another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 学会重建正常行为的神经网络，重建误差大即视为异常。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An autoencoder learns to reconstruct normal behavior and flags high reconstruction error as anomalous.
